title.zh: 卷二百五十七 列傳第十六 吳廷祚 李崇矩 王仁贍 楚昭輔 李處耘
title.en: Volume 257 Biographies 16: Wu Tingzuo, Li Chongju, Wang Renshan, Chu Zhaofu, Li Chuyun
title.raw: 卷二百五十七 列傳第十六 吳廷祚 李崇矩 王仁贍 楚昭輔 李處耘 Volume 257 Biographies 16: Wu Tingzuo, Li Chongju, Wang Renshan, Chu Zhaofu, Li Chuyun

sentences.zh: 吳廷祚

translations.literal: Wu Tingzuo
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingzuo

sentences.zh: 吳廷祚，字慶之，幷州太原人。

translations.literal: Wu Tingzuo, styled Qingzhi, was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingzuo, whose courtesy name was Qingzhi, came from Taiyuan in Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 少頗讀書，事周祖，為親校。

translations.literal: In youth he read considerably; he served the Zhou founder and became a personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied widely; he entered the service of the Zhou founder and served as a personal guard.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，授莊宅副使，遷內軍器庫使、知懷州，入為皇城使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangshun era he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Manor Estates, then promoted to Commissioner of the Inner Armory and acting prefect of Huaizhou, and entered the capital as Commissioner of the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun reign he received appointment as Vice Commissioner of the Manor Estates, was later transferred to Commissioner of the Inner Armory and acting prefect of Huaizhou, and then recalled to the capital as Commissioner of the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 會天平符彥卿移鎮大名，以廷祚權知鄆州。

translations.literal: When Fu Yanqing of the Tianping command was transferred to Da Ming, Tingzuo was appointed acting prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Yanqing of the Tianping command was reassigned to Da Ming, Tingzuo was put in temporary charge of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加同中書門下三品，以其父名璋，故避之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song he was given the rank of Tong zhongshu menxia sanpin, but because his father's name was Zhang he avoided using the full title.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Song he was granted the rank of Tong zhongshu menxia sanpin, but because his father's given name was Zhang he refrained from using the full form of the title.

sentences.zh: 會李筠叛，廷祚白太祖曰：「潞城岩險，且阻太行，賊據之，未易破也。

translations.literal: When Li Jing rebelled, Tingzuo told Taizu: "Lu City is precipitous and dangerous, and it blocks the Taihang range; with the rebels holding it, it will not be easy to break.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing rose in rebellion, Tingzuo reported to Taizu: "Lu City is rugged and commands the Taihang passes; while the rebels hold it, it will not be easy to reduce.

sentences.zh: 筠素勇而輕，若速擊之，必離上黨來邀我戰，猶獸亡其藪，魚脫於淵，因可擒矣。」

translations.literal: Jing has always been brave and rash; if we strike quickly he is sure to leave Shangdang to meet us in battle—like a beast that has lost its lair or a fish escaped from the deep—and then he can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Jing is by nature bold and reckless; if we attack at once he will certainly leave Shangdang to offer battle—as when a beast loses its den or a fish slips from the pool—and we can then take him."

sentences.zh: 太祖遂親征，以廷祚留守東京兼判開封府。

translations.literal: Taizu thereupon led the campaign in person and left Tingzuo to guard the Eastern Capital while also serving as acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then marched in person, leaving Tingzuo as defender of the Eastern Capital and acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 筠果領兵來，戰澤州南，其眾敗走。

translations.literal: Jing did indeed lead his troops out; they fought south of Ze Prefecture and his forces were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jing did lead his army forth; battle was joined south of Ze Prefecture, and his troops were routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 及討李重進，又為東京留守。

translations.literal: When Li Chongjin was suppressed he again served as defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Li Chongjin was undertaken, he again held the post of defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年夏，帝謂之曰：「卿掌樞務，有年於茲，與卿秦州，以均勞逸。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Jianlong the emperor said to him: "You have managed the pivot of state for many years here; I give you Qinzhou to balance labor and rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jianlong 2 the emperor told him: "You have long held the central duties of government at my side; I appoint you to Qinzhou to share the burden of service.

sentences.zh: 明日制出，恐卿以離朕左右為憂，故先告卿。」

translations.literal: The edict will issue tomorrow; fearing you might grieve at leaving my side, I tell you beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: The appointment will be promulgated tomorrow; lest you worry at being removed from my presence, I inform you in advance."

sentences.zh: 即以為雄武軍節度。

translations.literal: He was thereupon made military commissioner of the Xiongwu army.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately made military commissioner of the Xiongwu army.

sentences.zh: 先是，秦州夕陽鎮西北接大藪，多材植，古伏羌縣之地。

translations.literal: Earlier, northwest of Xiyang town in Qin Prefecture lay a great forest tract rich in timber—the site of the old Fuxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, northwest of Xiyang town in Qin Prefecture there adjoined a vast forest with abundant timber, on the ground of the ancient Fuxiang county.

sentences.zh: 高防知州日，建議就置采造務，調軍卒分番取其材以給京師。

translations.literal: When Gao Fang was prefect he proposed establishing a timber procurement office on the spot, drafting soldiers in rotating shifts to cut wood for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Gao Fang was prefect he proposed setting up a timber procurement office there and detailing troops in rotation to harvest timber for the capital.

sentences.zh: 西夏酋長尚波于率眾爭奪，頗傷役卒，防捕擊其黨，以狀聞。

translations.literal: The Western Xia chieftain Shang Boyu led his people to contest the cutting and many laborers were wounded; Fang seized his followers and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Xia chieftain Shang Boyu led his people to contest the timber, and many conscript laborers were hurt; Fang arrested his partisans and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 上令廷祚代防，齎詔赦尚波于等，夏人感悅。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Tingzuo to replace Fang, bearing an edict to pardon Shang Boyu and the rest; the Xia people were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Tingzuo to succeed Fang, carrying an edict pardoning Shang Boyu and his associates; the Xia were grateful and appeased.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，以伏羌地來獻。

translations.literal: That autumn they presented the Fuxiang territory in submission.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn they came forward and offered the Fuxiang territory in submission.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年來朝，改鎮京兆。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he came to court and was transferred to command Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 2 he came to court and was reassigned to command Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，長春節來朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao he came to court for the Changchun festival.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 4 he came to court for the Changchun festival.

sentences.zh: 俄遇疾，車駕臨問，命爇艾灸其腹，遣中使王繼恩監視之。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill; the imperial carriage visited him in person, ordered moxibustion on his abdomen, and sent the palace envoy Wang Jien to oversee the treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill; the emperor visited him in person, ordered cauterization of his abdomen, and dispatched the palace envoy Wang Jien to supervise the treatment.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he died, at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，官給葬事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant, and official funds were provided for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Palace Attendant, and the state supplied his funeral.

sentences.zh: 廷祚謹厚寡言，性至孝，居母喪，絕水漿累日。

translations.literal: Tingzuo was cautious, solid, and sparing of speech; by nature deeply filial—during his mother's mourning he went without food or drink for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzuo was prudent, reserved, and sparing of words; utterly filial by nature—while mourning his mother he abstained from food and drink for many days.

sentences.zh: 好學，聚書萬餘卷。

translations.literal: He loved learning and collected more than ten thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of study and amassed more than ten thousand volumes.

sentences.zh: 治家嚴肅，尤崇奉釋氏。

translations.literal: He governed his household with severity and especially revered Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: He ran his household with strict discipline and was especially devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 子元輔、元載、元範、元扆、元吉、元慶。

translations.literal: His sons were Yuanfu, Yuanzai, Yuanfan, Yuanyi, Yuanji, and Yuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yuanfu, Yuanzai, Yuanfan, Yuanyi, Yuanji, and Yuanqing.

sentences.zh: 元範、元慶仕皆至禮賓副使。

translations.literal: Yuanfan and Yuanqing both rose in office to Vice Commissioner of Ceremonial Reception.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfan and Yuanqing both attained the post of Vice Commissioner of Ceremonial Reception.

sentences.zh: 元吉，閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Yuanji served as Attendant of the Inner Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji served as Attendant of the Inner Gates.

sentences.zh: 元吉子昭允，太子中舍。

translations.literal: Yuanji's son Zhaoyun was a Middle Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji's son Zhaoyun held the post of Middle Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 元慶子守仁，內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Yuanqing's son Shouren was a Senior Officer of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing's son Shouren was a Senior Officer of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 子 元輔

translations.literal: Son: Yuanfu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yuanfu

sentences.zh: 元輔，字正臣，頗好學，善筆劄。

translations.literal: Yuanfu, styled Zhengchen, was quite fond of learning and skilled at correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu, whose courtesy name was Zhengchen, was studious and adept at letters.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，以父任補供奉官。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun period of Zhou he entered office through his father's position as a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhou Guangshun he received appointment through his father's privilege as a Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，遷洛苑使。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne he was transferred to Commissioner of the Luoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne he was made Commissioner of the Luoyuan.

sentences.zh: 宋初，授左驍衛將軍、澶州巡檢，累官至定州鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song he was made General of the Left Xiaoqi Guard and inspector of Cao Prefecture, rising in stages to military controller of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Song he was appointed General of the Left Xiaoqi Guard and inspector of Cao Prefecture, and eventually reached the post of military controller of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: He died, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子昭德、昭遜、昭普，並閤門祗候。

translations.literal: His sons Zhaode, Zhaoxun, and Zhaopu all served as Attendants of the Inner Gates.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhaode, Zhaoxun, and Zhaopu all served as Attendants of the Inner Gates.

sentences.zh: 子 元載

translations.literal: Son: Yuanzai
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yuanzai

sentences.zh: 元載，建隆初，授太子右春坊通事舍人，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: Yuanzai, at the beginning of Jianlong, was appointed Master of Ceremonies in the Right Spring Palace of the Heir Apparent and granted the crimson fish pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzai, at the start of Jianlong, was made Master of Ceremonies in the Right Spring Palace of the Heir Apparent and given the crimson fish pouch.

sentences.zh: 廷祚出鎮秦、雍，並補衙門都校。

translations.literal: When Tingzuo went out to command Qin and Yong, both were appointed chief guards of the yamen gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzuo took up command in Qin and Yong, both were appointed chief guards of the yamen gate.

sentences.zh: 廷祚卒，授供奉官。

translations.literal: When Tingzuo died he was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Tingzuo's death he was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，加閤門祗候，與太祝毋賓古使契丹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was made Attendant of the Inner Gates and, with Grand Invocator Wu Binggu, served as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 3 he was made Attendant of the Inner Gates and, with Grand Invocator Wu Binggu, went as envoy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢為西上閤門副使，出知陝州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Western Upper Inner Gates and sent out as prefect of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was elevated to Vice Commissioner of the Western Upper Inner Gates and appointed prefect of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，徙知秦州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he was transferred to prefect of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3 he was transferred to serve as prefect of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州民李益者，為長道縣酒務官，家饒於財，僮奴數千，指恣橫持郡吏短長，長吏而下皆畏之。

translations.literal: A townsman named Li Yi served as wine-tax officer of Changdao county; his household was wealthy, with thousands of slaves and servants, and he was wantonly overbearing, holding leverage over prefectural officials—everyone from the chief administrators down feared him.
translations.idiomatic: A resident named Li Yi held the wine monopoly post in Changdao county; his family was rich, with thousands of servants, and he acted with arrogant license, knowing the weaknesses of prefectural officials—magistrates and clerks alike feared him.

sentences.zh: 民負息錢者數百家，郡為督理如公家租調，獨推官馮伉不從。

translations.literal: Several hundred households owed him interest money; the prefecture collected it as it would state rent, but only the investigating officer Feng Kang refused.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred households owed him interest; the prefecture enforced collection as if it were official land tax, but only the investigating officer Feng Kang would not comply.

sentences.zh: 益遣奴數輩伺伉按行市中，拽之下馬，因毀辱之。

translations.literal: Yi sent several slaves to watch for Kang on his rounds in the market, dragged him from his horse, and humiliated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent several slaves to ambush Kang as he made his rounds in the market, pulled him from his horse, and publicly shamed him.

sentences.zh: 先是，益厚賂朝中權貴為庇護，故累年不敗。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yi had bribed powerful men at court for protection, and so for years he had not been brought down.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Yi had lavished bribes on powerful court figures for protection, and for years had escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 及伉屢表其事，又為邸吏所匿，不得達。

translations.literal: When Kang repeatedly memorialized the matter, courier clerks suppressed the reports and they never reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang repeatedly submitted memorials, postal clerks concealed them and they never reached the emperor.

sentences.zh: 後因市馬譯者附表以聞，譯因入見，上其表。

translations.literal: Later a horse-trading interpreter attached a memorial to his report; the interpreter entered audience and presented the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Later a horse-market interpreter carried a memorial with his dispatch; on entering audience he submitted it.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，詔元載逮捕之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered Yuanzai to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered Yuanzai to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 詔書未至，京師權貴已報益，益懼，亡命。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, powerful men in the capital had already informed Yi; in fear he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, capital magnates had already warned Yi; terrified, he absconded.

sentences.zh: 元載以聞，帝愈怒，詔州郡物色急捕之，獲於河中府民郝氏家，鞫於御史府，具得其狀，斬之，盡沒其家。

translations.literal: Yuanzai reported this; the emperor grew still angrier and ordered the prefectures to search urgently; he was seized at the home of a Mr. Hao in Hezhong Prefecture, tried in the Censorate, the full facts obtained, executed, and his entire property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzai reported upward; the emperor was still more enraged and ordered a manhunt throughout the circuits; Yi was taken at the home of a Mr. Hao in Hezhong Prefecture, examined in the Censorate, the case fully proved, beheaded, and his entire estate forfeited.

sentences.zh: 益子仕衡先舉進士，任光祿寺丞，詔除籍，終身不齒。

translations.literal: Yi's son Shihang had earlier passed the jinshi examination and served as Vice Director of the Imperial Household; an edict struck him from the rolls and he was never again received in official society.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Shihang had earlier passed the jinshi and served as Vice Director of the Imperial Household; an edict removed him from the registers, and he was excluded from office for life.

sentences.zh: 益之伏法，民皆飯僧相慶。

translations.literal: When Yi was executed the people all fed monks and celebrated together.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was put to death the people everywhere fed monks and rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遷西上閤門使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was transferred to Commissioner of the Western Upper Inner Gates.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Duangong he was made Commissioner of the Western Upper Inner Gates.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，加領富州刺史，俄徙知成都府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was additionally made prefect of Fuzhou and soon transferred to administer Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 2 he was additionally appointed prefect of Fuzhou and soon transferred to administer Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蜀俗奢侈，好遊蕩，民無贏餘，悉市酒肉為聲妓樂，元載禁止之；

translations.literal: Shu custom was extravagant and fond of dissipation; the people had no surplus and spent all on wine, meat, singing girls, and pleasure—Yuanzai forbade this;
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan custom was lavish and pleasure-loving; people had nothing left over and spent everything on wine, meat, singers, and entertainment—Yuanzai prohibited this;

sentences.zh: 吏民細罪又不少貸，人多怨咎。

translations.literal: petty offenses of officials and people he also rarely pardoned, and many resented and blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: minor offenses of officials and commoners he likewise seldom overlooked, and many bore grievances against him.

sentences.zh: 及王小波亂，元載不能捕滅，受代歸闕，而成都不守。

translations.literal: When Wang Xiaobo's rebellion broke out Yuanzai could not suppress it; he was replaced and returned to court, and Chengdu fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xiaobo's rebellion erupted Yuanzai could not put it down; he was relieved and recalled to court, and Chengdu was lost.

sentences.zh: 時李仕衡通判華州，常銜元載因事殺其父，伺元載至闕，遣人閱行裝，收其關市之稅。

translations.literal: At the time Li Shihang was acting prefect of Hua Prefecture and long resented Yuanzai for executing his father over the affair; when Yuanzai reached the capital he sent men to inspect his baggage and collect the market tolls.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Shihang was acting prefect of Hua Prefecture and had long harbored resentment because Yuanzai had put his father to death in the affair; when Yuanzai arrived at court, Shihang sent men to search his baggage and levy the market taxes.

sentences.zh: 元載拒之，仕衡抗章疏其罪，坐責郢州團練副使。

translations.literal: Yuanzai refused; Shihang submitted a forceful memorial detailing his crimes, and Yuanzai was demoted to vice military commissioner of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzai refused; Shihang submitted an accusatory memorial, and Yuanzai was punished by demotion to vice military commissioner of E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 移單州，以疾授左衛將軍致政。

translations.literal: He was moved to Shan Prefecture and, on grounds of illness, was granted the Left Guard General and retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shan Prefecture, he was granted the Left Guard General and retirement on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 子昭明，為內殿崇班；

translations.literal: His son Zhaoming was a Senior Officer of the Inner Hall;
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaoming was a Senior Officer of the Inner Hall;

sentences.zh: 昭矩，太子中舍。

translations.literal: Zhaoju was a Middle Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoju was a Middle Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子 元扆

translations.literal: Son: Yuanyi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yuanyi

sentences.zh: 元扆，字君華。

translations.literal: Yuanyi, styled Junhua.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi, whose courtesy name was Junhua.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，選尚太宗第四女蔡國公主，授左衛將軍、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he was chosen to marry Taizong's fourth daughter, Princess of the Cai State, and was made Left Guard General and Commissioner of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 8 he was selected to marry the fourth daughter of Taizong, Princess of Cai, and was appointed Left Guard General and Commissioner of the Imperial Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，領愛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he took charge as prefect of Ai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he assumed charge as prefect of Ai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是冬，領本州團練使。

translations.literal: That winter he took charge as regimental commander of his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he took charge as regimental commander of his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，有事北邊，元扆表求試劇郡，命知鄆州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, when there was trouble on the northern frontier, Yuanyi memorialized asking to try a demanding prefecture and was appointed prefect of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3, when affairs on the northern border were urgent, Yuanyi petitioned to test himself in a difficult prefecture and was appointed prefect of Yan.

sentences.zh: 逾年召入，尋知河陽。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled to court and soon made prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was recalled to court and soon made prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 還朝，改鄯州觀察使。

translations.literal: Returning to court he was made military governor of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made military governor of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 特詔朝會序班次節度使，奉祿賜予悉增之。

translations.literal: By special edict his place in court assembly was ranked with military commissioners, and his salary and gifts were all increased.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict ranked his place at court assemblies with military commissioners, and his salary and gifts were all increased.

sentences.zh: 再知河陽。

translations.literal: He again administered Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，以主疾召還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua he was recalled because the princess was ill.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 1 he was recalled because the princess fell ill.

sentences.zh: 主薨，復遣之任。

translations.literal: When the princess died he was again sent to his post.
translations.idiomatic: After the princess's death he was again dispatched to his post.

sentences.zh: 五年，秋霖河溢，奔注溝洫，城壘將壞，元扆躬涉泥滓，督工補塞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year autumn rains flooded the river, which poured into the ditches; the walls and ramparts were about to collapse—Yuanyi waded through the mud himself and supervised the workers in repair.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, autumn rains swelled the river and it rushed into the canals; the walls were near collapse—Yuanyi waded through the mire himself and directed the laborers in repairs.

sentences.zh: 民多構木樹杪以避水，元扆命濟以舟楫，設餅餌以食。

translations.literal: Many people built platforms in treetops to escape the water; Yuanyi ordered them ferried by boat and provided cakes and food.
translations.idiomatic: Many people built platforms in treetops to escape the flood; Yuanyi had them ferried by boat and set out cakes and food.

sentences.zh: 時澶、陝悉罹水災，元扆所部賴以獲安。

translations.literal: At the time Cao and Shan both suffered flood disaster, but Yuanyi's jurisdiction was preserved in safety.
translations.idiomatic: Cao and Shan were then both stricken by flood, but the region under Yuanyi was kept safe.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，換安州觀察使，俄知澶州。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne he was transferred to military governor of An Prefecture and soon made prefect of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong came to the throne he was transferred to military governor of An Prefecture and soon made prefect of Cao.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，轉運使劉錫上其治狀，詔書嘉獎，遷寧國軍留後、知定州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping the transport commissioner Liu Xi reported on his administration; an edict praised him and he was promoted to regent of the Ningguo army and prefect of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3 transport commissioner Liu Xi reported on his governance; an edict commended him and he was promoted to regent of the Ningguo army and prefect of Ding.

sentences.zh: 時王超、王繼忠領兵逾唐河，與遼人戰，元扆度其必敗，乃急發州兵護河橋。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Chao and Wang Jizhong led troops across the Tang River to fight the Liao; Yuanyi judged they would certainly be defeated and urgently dispatched prefectural troops to guard the river bridge.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Chao and Wang Jizhong led troops across the Tang River to fight the Liao; Yuanyi foresaw defeat and urgently sent prefectural troops to hold the river bridge.

sentences.zh: 既而超輩果敗，遼人乘之，至橋，見陣兵甚盛，遂引去。

translations.literal: Soon after, Wang and his fellows were indeed defeated; the Liao pressed the pursuit to the bridge, saw the array of troops very strong, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang and his fellows were indeed beaten; the Liao pressed after them to the bridge, saw a formidable formation, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 考滿，吏民詣闕貢馬，疏其善政十事，願借留樹碑，表其德政。

translations.literal: When his term ended officials and people went to court to present horses, listing ten items of good government, and asked that he be retained and a stele erected to record his virtuous administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term officials and people went to court with horses, set forth ten acts of good government, and asked that he be kept on and a monument raised to his virtuous rule.

sentences.zh: 詔褒之。

translations.literal: An edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 屬歲旱，吏白召巫以土龍請雨。

translations.literal: During a year of drought the clerks reported that shamans should be summoned and an earthen dragon used to pray for rain.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of drought the clerks proposed summoning shamans and using an earthen dragon to pray for rain.

sentences.zh: 元扆曰：「巫本妖民，龍止獸也，安能格天？

translations.literal: Yuanyi said: "Shamans are by nature delusive people, and a dragon is only a beast—how can they reach Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi said: "Shamans are deceitful by nature, and a dragon is merely an animal—how can they move Heaven?

sentences.zh: 惟精誠可以動天。」

translations.literal: Only sincerity can move Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Only sincerity can move Heaven."

sentences.zh: 乃集道人設壇，潔齋三日，百拜祈禱，澍雨沾洽。

translations.literal: He then gathered Daoist masters, set up an altar, kept pure fast for three days, bowed a hundred times in prayer, and soaking rain fell abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: He then assembled Daoist masters, set up an altar, kept a pure fast for three days, bowed a hundred times in supplication, and a soaking rain fell in abundance.

sentences.zh: 景德三年代歸，拜武勝軍節度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde he was replaced and returned, and was made military commissioner of the Wusheng army.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 3 he was relieved and returned, and was appointed military commissioner of the Wusheng army.

sentences.zh: 三年，以陵域積水，議堙掘溝澗，命為修諸陵都部署，以內侍副都知閻承翰副之。

translations.literal: In the third year, because the imperial tombs had standing water, it was proposed to fill in and dig out gullies and ravines; he was appointed overall director for repairing the imperial tombs, with Vice Director of the Inner Service Yan Chenghan as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, because the imperial tombs had accumulated water, filling and excavation of gullies was proposed; he was made overall director for repairing the imperial tombs, with Vice Director of the Inner Service Yan Chenghan as deputy.

sentences.zh: 出知潞州。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，幷、代、澤、潞皆分轄戍卒，後並於太原。

translations.literal: Initially Bing, Dai, Ze, and Lu each had separate garrisons; later they were consolidated at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At first Bing, Dai, Ze, and Lu each had separate garrisons; later they were combined at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 至是，以元扆臨鎮，遂分領澤、潞、晉、絳、磁、隰、威勝七州軍戎事，委元扆專總之。

translations.literal: Now, with Yuanyi governing the region, military affairs of the seven prefectures and commands—Ze, Lu, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, and Weisheng—were divided under him and entrusted to his sole command.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, with Yuanyi in command of the region, military affairs of the seven prefectures and commands—Ze, Lu, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, and Weisheng—were divided under him and entrusted to his overall direction.

sentences.zh: 東封，表求扈從，命祀青帝。

translations.literal: On the eastern feng sacrifice he memorialized asking to attend in escort and was ordered to sacrifice to the Green Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern feng rite he petitioned to accompany the procession and was ordered to offer sacrifice to the Green Emperor.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，加檢校太傅、知徐州。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was made Honorary Grand Tutor and prefect of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished he was made Honorary Grand Tutor and prefect of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，以祀汾陰恩，改領山南東道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, by grace of the Fenyin sacrifice he was transferred to command the Shannan East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 4, by grace of the Fenyin sacrifice he was reassigned to command the Shannan East circuit.

sentences.zh: 五月，制書下，元扆被疾卒，年五十。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the appointment edict was issued; Yuanyi, stricken with illness, died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the edict was promulgated; Yuanyi fell ill and died, at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令，諡忠惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Councilor and given the posthumous title Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Grand Councilor, with the posthumous title Zhonghui (Loyal and Kind).

sentences.zh: 子弟進秩者五人。

translations.literal: Five of his sons and younger relatives were advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five of his sons and younger kinsmen were promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，葬元扆，時上元欲觀燈，帝為移次夕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Yuanyi was buried, the Lantern Festival was near; the emperor postponed the viewing of lanterns by one evening.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, at Yuanyi's burial, the Upper Yuan lantern viewing was imminent; the emperor moved it to the following evening.

sentences.zh: 元扆性謹讓，在帆鎮有憂民心，待賓佐以禮。

translations.literal: Yuanyi was by nature cautious and modest; in his postings he showed concern for the people and treated his staff with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi was prudent and self-effacing; in his commands he cared for the people and treated his aides with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 喜讀《春秋左氏》，聲色狗馬，一不介意。

translations.literal: He delighted in reading the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and cared not at all for music, women, or horses.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and took no interest in sensual pleasures or sport.

sentences.zh: 所得祿賜，即給親族孤貧者。

translations.literal: Whatever salary and gifts he received he at once gave to poor kinsmen and the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: His salary and gifts he immediately distributed to needy kinsmen and the poor.

sentences.zh: 將赴徐州，請對言：「臣族屬至多，其堪祿仕者皆為表薦，餘皆均奉贍之。」

translations.literal: When about to go to Xu Prefecture he requested audience and said: "My clan is very large; those fit for office I have all recommended by memorial; the rest I support equally from my income."
translations.idiomatic: Before departing for Xu Prefecture he sought audience and said: "My clan is numerous; those qualified for office I have all recommended; the remainder I support equally from my stipend."

sentences.zh: 公主有乳媼，得入參宮禁，元扆慮其去後妄有請托，白上拒之。

translations.literal: The princess had a wet nurse who was allowed to enter the palace; Yuanyi feared that after his departure she might make improper requests, and reported to the throne to refuse them.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had a nurse who could enter the inner palace; fearing she might seek improper favors after his departure, Yuanyi asked the emperor to refuse them.

sentences.zh: 真宗深所嘉歎，於帝婿中獨稱其賢。

translations.literal: Zhenzong greatly admired this and among the imperial sons-in-law singled him out alone as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong greatly praised this and among the emperor's sons-in-law named him alone as worthy.

sentences.zh: 及歿，甚悼惜之。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor deeply mourned and regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor deeply mourned him.

sentences.zh: 且以元扆得疾，本州不以聞，詔劾其官屬。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Yuanyi had fallen ill and the prefecture had not reported it, an edict censured his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuanyi's illness had not been reported by the prefecture, an edict punished his officials.

sentences.zh: 子守禮，至六宅使、澄州刺史，以帝甥特贈和州防禦使；

translations.literal: His son Shouli rose to Commissioner of the Six Residences and prefect of Cheng Prefecture; as the emperor's nephew he was specially posthumously made defender of He Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouli reached Commissioner of the Six Residences and prefect of Cheng; as the emperor's nephew he was specially posthumously made defender of He Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 守嚴，至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Shouyan reached Senior Officer of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyan rose to Senior Officer of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，錄守嚴子承嗣、承緒並為殿直；

translations.literal: In the Tianxi era Shouyan's sons Chengsi and Chengxu were both enrolled as Palace Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianxi period Shouyan's sons Chengsi and Chengxu were both made Palace Attendants;

sentences.zh: 守良為內殿崇班；

translations.literal: Shouliang was a Senior Officer of the Inner Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Shouliang was a Senior Officer of the Inner Hall;

sentences.zh: 守讓閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Shourang was Attendant of the Inner Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Shourang was Attendant of the Inner Gates.

sentences.zh: 李崇矩

translations.literal: Li Chongju
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongju

sentences.zh: 李崇矩，字守則，潞州上黨人。

translations.literal: Li Chongju, styled Shouze, was a native of Shangdang in Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongju, whose courtesy name was Shouze, came from Shangdang in Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧，有至行，鄉里推服。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he had supreme conduct and the village respected and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth and poor, he showed exemplary conduct and his neighbors looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 漢祖起晉陽，次上黨，史弘肇時為先鋒都校，聞崇矩名，召署親吏。

translations.literal: When the Han founder rose at Jinyang and halted at Shangdang, Shi Hongzhao was then vanguard commander; hearing Chongju's name, he summoned him and appointed him a personal clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder rose at Jinyang and camped at Shangdang, Shi Hongzhao was vanguard commander; hearing of Chongju, he summoned him as a personal clerk.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，弘肇總禁兵兼京城巡檢，多殘殺軍民，左右懼，稍稍引去，惟崇矩事之益謹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou, Hongzhao commanded the forbidden army and also inspected the capital, killing many soldiers and civilians; his attendants feared him and gradually withdrew—only Chongju served him with growing care.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou, Hongzhao commanded the forbidden troops and patrolled the capital, killing many soldiers and civilians; his attendants feared him and drifted away—only Chongju served him with increasing devotion.

sentences.zh: 及弘肇被誅，獨得免。

translations.literal: When Hongzhao was executed he alone escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhao was put to death he alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 周祖與弘肇素厚善，即位，訪求弘肇親舊，得崇矩。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder had long been close to Hongzhao; on taking the throne he sought Hongzhao's kin and associates and found Chongju.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder had been on close terms with Hongzhao; on his accession he sought Hongzhao's kin and found Chongju.

sentences.zh: 謂之曰：「我與史公受漢厚恩，戳力同心，共獎王室，為奸邪所構，史公卒罹大禍，我亦僅免。

translations.literal: He said to him: "Lord Shi and I received great favor from the Han, exerted ourselves with one heart, and together supported the royal house; we were framed by wicked men, and Lord Shi finally suffered great calamity while I barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He told him: "Lord Shi and I owed deep debts to the Han, labored together in one purpose, and upheld the throne; villains set us at odds, Lord Shi met a great disaster, and I barely survived.

sentences.zh: 汝史氏家故吏也，為我求其近屬，吾將恤之。」

translations.literal: You are an old retainer of the Shi household; find his near kin for me and I will show them favor."
translations.idiomatic: You are an old servant of the Shi family; seek out his close kin for me and I will care for them."

sentences.zh: 崇矩上其母弟福。

translations.literal: Chongju presented Hongzhao's younger brother by the same mother, Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Chongju presented Hongzhao's uterine younger brother Fu.

sentences.zh: 崇矩素主其家，盡籍財產以付福，周祖嘉之，以崇矩隸世宗帳下。

translations.literal: Chongju had long managed the household; he inventoried all property and handed it to Fu; the Zhou founder commended this and placed Chongju under Shizong's command.
translations.idiomatic: Chongju had long managed the household; he registered all assets and delivered them to Fu; the Zhou founder praised this and assigned Chongju to Shizong's staff.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，補供奉官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was made a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiande he was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從征高平，以功轉供備庫副使，改作坊使。

translations.literal: On the Gaoping campaign he was transferred for merit to Vice Commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Store and then made Commissioner of the Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: On the Gaoping campaign he was promoted for merit to Vice Commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Store and then made Commissioner of the Workshops.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，命崇矩告哀於南唐。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne Chongju was ordered to announce the mourning to Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Chongju was sent to announce the mourning to Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 還判四方館事。

translations.literal: On his return he was put in charge of the Four Directions Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was placed in charge of the Four Directions Hostel.

sentences.zh: 宋初，李筠叛，命崇矩率龍捷、驍武左右射禁軍數千人屯河陽，以所部攻大會砦，拔之，斬首五百級。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, when Li Jing rebelled, Chongju was ordered to lead several thousand men of the Longjie and Xiaowu Left and Right Archer forbidden troops to garrison Heyang; with his command he attacked the Great Assembly stockade, took it, and beheaded five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, when Li Jing rebelled, Chongju was ordered to lead several thousand Longjie and Xiaowu archer guards to garrison Heyang; he attacked the Great Assembly stockade, captured it, and took five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 改澤、潞南面行營前軍都監，與石守信、高懷德、羅彥瓌同破筠眾於碾子谷。

translations.literal: He was made chief controller of the vanguard of the southern Ze-Lu campaign army and, with Shi Shouxin, Gao Huaide, and Luo Yanqiong, jointly broke Jing's forces at Nianzi Valley.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief controller of the vanguard of the southern Ze-Lu campaign and, with Shi Shouxin, Gao Huaide, and Luo Yanqiong, defeated Jing's army at Nianzi Valley.

sentences.zh: 及平澤、潞，遣崇矩先入城，收圖籍，視府庫。

translations.literal: When Ze and Lu were pacified he was sent ahead into the city to collect registers and inspect the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: When Ze and Lu were pacified he was sent first into the city to gather registers and inspect the treasuries.

sentences.zh: 因上言曰：「上黨，臣鄉里也。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized: "Shangdang is my native place.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized: "Shangdang is my home district.

sentences.zh: 臣父尚槀葬，願護櫬歸京師。」

translations.literal: My father's coffin is still unburied; I beg leave to escort the bier to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: My father's coffin remains above ground; I ask to escort it to the capital."

sentences.zh: 許之，賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: Permission was granted and the gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted and the rewards were lavish.

sentences.zh: 師還，會判三司張美出鎮，拜右監門衛大將軍，充三司使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, as Zhang Mei, acting head of the Three Departments, went out to a command, Chongju was made Grand General of the Right Jianmen Guard and appointed head of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, as Zhang Mei of the Three Departments went out to command a circuit, Chongju was made Grand General of the Right Jianmen Guard and head of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 從征李重進，還為宣徽北院使，仍判三司。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Li Chongjin he returned as Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and still headed the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Li Chongjin he returned as Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and continued to head the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，代趙普拜樞密使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he succeeded Zhao Pu as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 2 he replaced Zhao Pu as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 時劍南初平，禁軍校呂翰聚眾構亂，軍多亡命在其黨中，言者請誅其妻子。

translations.literal: At the time the Sword South had just been pacified; forbidden-army officer Lu Han gathered a crowd and raised rebellion, and many deserters were in his party; memorialists asked that their wives and children be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sword South had just been pacified, forbidden-army officer Lu Han gathered followers and rebelled, and many deserters were among them; officials proposed executing their families.

sentences.zh: 太祖疑之，以語崇矩。

translations.literal: Taizu was doubtful and spoke of it to Chongju.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was uncertain and consulted Chongju.

sentences.zh: 崇矩曰：「叛亡之徒固當孥戮，然案籍合誅者萬餘人。」

translations.literal: Chongju said: "Rebels and fugitives ought indeed to have their families punished, yet according to the registers more than ten thousand would be liable to execution."
translations.idiomatic: Chongju said: "Deserters should indeed have their kin punished, but the registers show more than ten thousand liable to death."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「朕恐有被其驅率，非本心者。」

translations.literal: Taizu said: "I fear some were driven by others and did not act from their own hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said: "I fear some were coerced and did not act willingly."

sentences.zh: 乃令盡釋之。

translations.literal: He then ordered them all released.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered them all freed.

sentences.zh: 翰眾聞之，亦稍稍自歸。

translations.literal: When Han's followers heard this they too gradually returned of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Han's followers heard this they gradually came back on their own.

sentences.zh: 未幾，翰敗滅。

translations.literal: Before long Han was defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Han was defeated and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，從征太原。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao he followed the campaign against Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaibao he joined the campaign against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 會班師，命崇矩為後殿。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew he was ordered to command the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew he was ordered to command the rearguard.

sentences.zh: 次常山，被病，帝遣太醫診視，命乘涼車還京師。

translations.literal: Halting at Changshan he fell ill; the emperor sent the imperial physician to examine him and ordered him to ride the cool carriage back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Changshan he fell ill; the emperor sent the court physician and ordered him to return in the imperial cool carriage.

sentences.zh: 崇矩叩頭言：「涼車乃至尊所御，是速臣死爾。」

translations.literal: Chongju kowtowed and said: "The cool carriage is what Your Majesty himself rides—it would hasten this servant's death."
translations.idiomatic: Chongju kowtowed and said: "The cool carriage is reserved for Your Majesty—it would only hasten my death."

sentences.zh: 固辭得免。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and was excused.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused and was spared.

sentences.zh: 時趙普為相，崇矩以女妻普子承宗，相厚善，帝聞之不悅。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Pu was chief councilor; Chongju gave his daughter in marriage to Pu's son Chengzong and they were on close terms—the emperor heard of it and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu was then chief councilor; Chongju married his daughter to Pu's son Chengzong and they were intimate—the emperor heard of it and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 有鄭伸者，客崇矩門下僅十年，性險詖無行，崇矩待之漸薄。

translations.literal: There was a Zheng Shen who had been a client at Chongju's gate for nearly ten years—treacherous, deceitful, and without conduct—and Chongju treated him with growing coldness.
translations.idiomatic: A client named Zheng Shen had stayed at Chongju's house nearly ten years; treacherous and without principle, he was treated with growing neglect.

sentences.zh: 伸銜之，因上書告崇矩陰事。

translations.literal: Shen harbored resentment and submitted a memorial accusing Chongju of secret misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Shen bore a grudge and memorialized accusing Chongju of secret wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 崇矩不能自明。

translations.literal: Chongju could not clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chongju could not exonerate himself.

sentences.zh: 太祖釋不問，出為鎮國軍節度，賜伸同進士出身，以為酸棗主簿；

translations.literal: Taizu released the matter without inquiry, sent him out as military commissioner of the Zhenguo army, granted Shen status as a jinshi graduate, and made him recorder of Suanzao;
translations.idiomatic: Taizu dismissed the matter, sent Chongju out as military commissioner of the Zhenguo army, granted Shen jinshi status, and made him recorder of Suanzao;

sentences.zh: 仍賜器幣、襲衣、銀帶。

translations.literal: he also bestowed vessels, coins, ceremonial dress, and a silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: he also gave Shen ritual vessels, coins, court dress, and a silver belt.

sentences.zh: 六年，崇矩入為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Chongju entered the capital as Grand General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Chongju returned to the capital as Grand General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 崇矩性純厚寡言，尤重然諾。

translations.literal: Chongju was by nature pure, thick, and sparing of speech, and especially valued his promises.
translations.idiomatic: Chongju was sincere, reserved, and sparing of words, and set great store by his word.

sentences.zh: 嘗事史弘肇，及卒，見其子孫，必厚禮之，振其乏絕。

translations.literal: He had once served Shi Hongzhao; when Hongzhao died, whenever he met his descendants he always treated them generously and relieved their want.
translations.idiomatic: He had served Shi Hongzhao; after Hongzhao's death, whenever he met his descendants he honored them and aided their poverty.

sentences.zh: 在嶺海四五年，恬不以炎荒嬰慮。

translations.literal: During four or five years in Linghai he was untroubled by the southern heat.
translations.idiomatic: For four or five years in the Lingnan coast he was untroubled by the tropical climate.

sentences.zh: 舊涉海者多艤舟以俟便風，或旬餘，或彌月，崇矩往來皆一日而渡，未嘗留滯，士卒僮僕隨者皆無恙。

translations.literal: Formerly those crossing the sea often moored to await favorable winds—for ten days or more, or a full month; Chongju's crossings were all made in a single day without delay, and the soldiers and servants who accompanied him were all unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers on the sea formerly waited weeks for fair winds; Chongju always crossed in a day without delay, and all who followed him were unharmed.

sentences.zh: 信奉釋氏，飯僧至七十萬，造像建寺尤多。

translations.literal: He believed in Buddhism, fed monks to the number of seven hundred thousand, and especially built many images and temples.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to Buddhism, fed seven hundred thousand monks, and especially erected many images and temples.

sentences.zh: 又喜黃白術，自遠迎其人，館於家以師之，雖知其詐，猶以為神仙，試已終無悔恨。

translations.literal: He also delighted in alchemical arts; he welcomed practitioners from afar, lodged them at home as teachers, and though he knew they deceived him still regarded them as immortals—when the experiments failed he never regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He also pursued alchemical arts, welcomed adepts from afar, and housed them as masters; though he knew they were frauds he still treated them as immortals and never regretted the trials.

sentences.zh: 子繼昌。

translations.literal: His son was Jichang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jichang.

sentences.zh: 子 繼昌

translations.literal: Son: Jichang
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jichang

sentences.zh: 繼昌，字世長。

translations.literal: Jichang, styled Shichang.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang, whose courtesy name was Shichang.

sentences.zh: 初，崇矩與太祖同府厚善，每太祖誕辰，必遣繼昌奉幣為壽。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chongju and Taizu had been close in the same office; every year on Taizu's birthday he would send Jichang with gifts to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Chongju and Taizu had long been close colleagues; each year on Taizu's birthday he sent Jichang with gifts of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 嘗畀弱弓輕矢，教以射法。

translations.literal: He once gave him a weak bow and light arrows and taught him archery.
translations.idiomatic: He once gave him a light bow and taught him to shoot.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，蔭補西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he entered office by privilege as Attendant of the Western Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 3 he entered office by privilege as Attendant of the Western Gate.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲選尚公主，崇矩謙讓不敢當，繼昌亦自言不願。

translations.literal: Taizu wished to choose him to marry a princess; Chongju modestly declined to accept it and Jichang himself said he was unwilling.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wished to marry him to a princess; Chongju humbly declined and Jichang said he did not wish it.

sentences.zh: 崇矩亟為繼昌聘婦，太祖聞之，頗不悅。

translations.literal: Chongju hastened to arrange a marriage for Jichang; when Taizu heard of it he was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Chongju quickly betrothed Jichang; when Taizu learned of it he was much displeased.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，選魏咸信為駙馬都尉，繼昌同日遷如京副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao Wei Xianxin was chosen as Commissioner of the Imperial Son-in-Law, and Jichang was promoted the same day to Vice Commissioner of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 5 Wei Xianxin was made Commissioner of the Imperial Son-in-Law, and Jichang was promoted the same day to Vice Commissioner of the Capital.

sentences.zh: 崇矩出華州，補鎮國軍牙職。

translations.literal: When Chongju went out to Hua Prefecture, Jichang was appointed to the Zhenguo army yamen staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongju went to Hua Prefecture, Jichang was appointed to the Zhenguo army staff.

sentences.zh: 入為右班殿直、東頭供奉官，監大名府商稅，歲課增羨。

translations.literal: He entered service as Right-Ban Palace Attendant and Eastern-Gate Attendant, supervised the commercial tax of Daming Prefecture, and the annual receipts increased.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right-Ban Palace Attendant and Eastern-Gate Attendant, supervised Daming's commercial tax, and annual revenue increased.

sentences.zh: 會詔擇廷臣有勞者，府以名聞。

translations.literal: When an edict chose court officials of merit the prefecture submitted his name.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sought meritorious officials the prefecture nominated him.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，服闋，授西京作坊副使。

translations.literal: After his father's mourning and the end of mourning he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，齊饑多盜，命為登、萊、沂、密七州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era Qi suffered famine and many bandits; he was made overall inspector of Deng, Lai, Yi, and Mi and seven other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua Qi suffered famine and banditry; he was made overall inspector of Deng, Lai, Yi, Mi, and seven other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，蜀賊平，餘黨頗嘯聚，拜西京作坊使、峽路二十五州軍捉賊招安都巡檢使，旋改兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, when Shu rebels were pacified but remnants still gathered, he was made Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and overall inspector for capturing bandits and pacifying the twenty-five prefectures and commands of the Gorges route, soon changed to military controller.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 2, when Shu was pacified but remnants remained, he was made Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and overall bandit-suppression inspector of the twenty-five Gorges prefectures, soon made military controller.

sentences.zh: 賊酋喻雷燒者，久為民患，以金帶遺繼昌，繼昌偽納之，賊懈不設備，因掩殺之。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Yu Leishao had long been a scourge to the people; he sent Jichang a gold belt; Jichang pretended to accept it, the bandits relaxed their guard, and he attacked and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chief Yu Leishao had long plagued the people; he sent Jichang a gold belt; Jichang feigned acceptance, the bandits lowered their guard, and he destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 進西京左藏庫使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，王均亂蜀，與雷有終、上官正、石普同受詔進討，砦於城西門。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, when Wang Jun rebelled in Shu, he received orders with Lei Youzhong, Shangguan Zheng, and Shi Pu to advance against him and encamped at the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3, when Wang Jun rebelled in Shu, he joined Lei Youzhong, Shangguan Zheng, and Shi Pu to attack and encamped at the west gate.

sentences.zh: 賊忽開城偽遁，有終等各以所部徑入，繼昌覺，亟止之不聽，因獨還砦。

translations.literal: The rebels suddenly opened the gate in feigned flight; Youzhong and the others each led their commands straight in; Jichang perceived the trap and urgently tried to stop them but was not heeded, and alone returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels opened the gate in a false retreat; Youzhong and the others led their troops straight in; Jichang sensed the trap, tried to halt them in vain, and alone returned to camp.

sentences.zh: 賊果閉關發伏，悉陷之，有終等僅以身免。

translations.literal: The rebels indeed closed the gate and sprang an ambush; all were trapped; Youzhong and the others barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shut the gate and sprang an ambush; nearly all were lost; Youzhong and the others barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 繼昌按堵如故，所部諸校聞城中戰聲，泣請引去。

translations.literal: Jichang held his position as before; the officers under him, hearing battle in the city, wept and begged to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang held his camp steady; his officers, hearing fighting in the city, wept and begged to retreat.

sentences.zh: 繼昌曰：「吾位最下，當俟主帥命。」

translations.literal: Jichang said: "My rank is lowest; I must await the commander's order."
translations.idiomatic: Jichang said: "I am lowest in rank; I must wait for the commander's order."

sentences.zh: 是夕，有終馳報至，徙繼昌屯雁橋門。

translations.literal: That evening Youzhong's urgent report arrived and Jichang was moved to camp at the Wild Goose Bridge gate.
translations.idiomatic: That night Youzhong's dispatch arrived and Jichang was shifted to camp at the Wild Goose Bridge gate.

sentences.zh: 三月，破彌牟砦，斬首千級，大獲器仗，進逼魚橋門，均脫走。

translations.literal: In the third month they broke the Mimu stockade, beheaded a thousand, seized great stores of weapons, pressed on to the Fish Bridge gate, and Jun fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they stormed the Mimu stockade, took a thousand heads and much booty, pressed to the Fish Bridge gate, and Jun fled.

sentences.zh: 繼昌入城，嚴戒部下，無擾民者。

translations.literal: Jichang entered the city and strictly warned his men not to disturb the people.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang entered the city and strictly forbade his troops to harm the people.

sentences.zh: 獲婦女童幼置空寺中，俟事平遣還其家。

translations.literal: Captured women and children he placed in empty temples and, when affairs were settled, sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: Women and children taken captive he placed in empty temples and sent home when order was restored.

sentences.zh: 繼昌急領兵追賊至資州，聞均梟首乃還。

translations.literal: Jichang hurriedly led troops in pursuit to Zi Prefecture and returned only on hearing that Jun's head had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang pursued the rebels to Zi Prefecture and returned only when Jun's head was reported taken.

sentences.zh: 以功領獎州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made acting prefect of Jiao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made acting prefect of Jiao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄知青州，入掌軍頭引見司。

translations.literal: Soon he was prefect of Qing Prefecture and entered to head the Army Head Presentation Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was prefect of Qing and entered to head the Army Head Presentation Office.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，將幸澶州，遣先赴河上給諸軍鎧甲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, when the emperor was about to visit Cao Prefecture, he was sent ahead to the river to supply armor to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 2, when the emperor planned to visit Cao, he was sent ahead to the Yellow River to issue armor to the armies.

sentences.zh: 遼人請和，欲近臣充使，乃令繼昌與其使姚東之偕詣遼部，俄與韓杞同至行在；

translations.literal: When the Liao sought peace and wished a near minister as envoy, he was ordered to go with their envoy Yao Dongzhi to the Liao territory; soon he returned with Han Qi to the imperial camp;
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao sought peace and wanted a senior courtier as envoy, he went with their envoy Yao Dongzhi to the Liao border and soon returned with Han Qi to the imperial camp;

sentences.zh: 及遼人聘至，又命至境首接伴。

translations.literal: when Liao envoys came on a mission he was again ordered to meet them first at the border as chief escort.
translations.idiomatic: when Liao envoys arrived he was again ordered to receive them first at the border as chief escort.

sentences.zh: 尋擢為西上閤門使。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.

sentences.zh: 三年，又副任中正使契丹。

translations.literal: In the third year he again served as deputy chief envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he again served as deputy chief envoy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 是冬，將朝陵寢，以汝州近洛，衛兵所駐，命知州事兼兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: That winter, when the emperor was to attend the imperial tombs, because Ruzhou was near Luoyang and where the guard troops were stationed, he was ordered to administer the prefecture and also serve as military controller.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, as the emperor was to visit the tombs, Ruzhou being near Luoyang and the guard encampment, he was ordered to govern the prefecture and serve as military controller.

sentences.zh: 駕還，召歸，出知延州兼鄜延路鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned he was recalled, then sent out as prefect of Yanzhou and military controller of the Fuyan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned he was recalled, then made prefect of Yanzhou and military controller of the Fuyan circuit.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，主誕日，邀繼昌過其家，迎拜為壽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, on the princess's birthday she invited Jichang to her home and received him with bows to wish her long life.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianxi, on the princess's birthday she invited Jichang to her home and received him with birthday obeisances.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，密以襲衣、金帶、器幣、珍果、美饌賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it and secretly sent him robes, a gold belt, vessels and silks, rare fruits, and fine food.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of it and secretly sent robes, a gold belt, vessels, silks, rare fruits, and delicacies.

sentences.zh: 翌日，主入對，帝問繼昌強健能飲食，拜連州刺史，出知涇州。

translations.literal: The next day the princess entered audience; the emperor asked whether Jichang was strong and able to eat and drink, enfeoffed him as prefect of Lianzhou, and sent him out as prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the princess had audience; the emperor asked after Jichang's health, made him prefect of Lianzhou, and sent him to govern Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 表求兩朝御書及謁拜諸陵，皆許之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting imperial writings of both reigns and permission to visit the tombs; all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He requested imperial calligraphy from both reigns and leave to visit the tombs; all was granted.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year he died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 遣中使護櫬以歸。

translations.literal: An inner envoy was sent to escort the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial envoy escorted his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 錄其子讚善大夫文晟為殿中丞，殿直文旦為侍禁。

translations.literal: His son Wensheng, Gentleman for Fostering Virtue, was recorded as Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; Wendant, Palace Attendant, as Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wensheng, Gentleman for Fostering Virtue, was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; Wendant, Palace Attendant, became Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 繼昌性謹厚，士大夫樂與之遊。

translations.literal: Jichang was by nature careful and generous; scholar-officials delighted in his company.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang was careful and generous; scholar-officials were glad to associate with him.

sentences.zh: 為治尚寬，所至民懷之。

translations.literal: In governing he favored leniency; wherever he went the people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed leniently; the people cherished him wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 任峽路時，與上官正聯職。

translations.literal: While on the Gorges route he served alongside Shangguan Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the Gorges route he served with Shangguan Zheng.

sentences.zh: 正殘忍好殺，嘗有縣胥護芻糧，地遠後期，正令斬之，繼昌徐為解貸焉。

translations.literal: Zheng was cruel and fond of killing; once a county clerk escorting fodder, because the place was remote, was late; Zheng ordered him beheaded; Jichang slowly secured his pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was cruel and bloodthirsty; once a county clerk escorting fodder was late because of the distance, and Zheng ordered him beheaded; Jichang gradually secured his release.

sentences.zh: 鄭伸者，早死，其母貧餓，嘗詣繼昌乞丐，家人兢前詬逐。

translations.literal: Zheng Shen had died early; his mother was poor and hungry and once came to Jichang to beg; the household rushed forward to revile and drive her off.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shen had died young; his mother, poor and starving, came to beg from Jichang; the household rushed out to abuse and drive her away.

sentences.zh: 繼昌召見，與白金百兩，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Jichang summoned her in and gave her a hundred taels of white silver; people praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang received her and gave her a hundred taels of silver; people praised him.

sentences.zh: 遵勖初尚主，詔升為崇矩子，授昭德軍留後、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Zunxu first married the princess, an edict raised him to be Chongju's son and appointed him military commissioner of the Zhaode army and Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zunxu first married the princess, an edict made him Chongju's son and appointed him military commissioner of Zhaode and Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant.

sentences.zh: 王仁贍

translations.literal: Wang Renshan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renshan

sentences.zh: 王仁贍，唐州方城人。

translations.literal: Wang Renshan was a native of Fangcheng in Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renshan was from Fangcheng in Tang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，不事生產，委質刺史劉詞。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited and did not attend to production; he offered his service to the prefect Liu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and idle; he entered the service of Prefect Liu Ci.

sentences.zh: 詞遷永興節度，署為牙校。

translations.literal: When Ci was transferred to the Yongxing command he appointed him a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci became military commissioner of Yongxing he made him a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 詞將卒，遺表薦仁贍材可用。

translations.literal: As Ci was dying he left a memorial recommending Renshan's talent as usable.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Ci memorialized that Renshan's talent should be used.

sentences.zh: 太祖素知其名，請於世宗，以隸帳下。

translations.literal: Taizu had long known his name and requested him from Shizong to place under his own command.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had long known his name and asked Shizong to assign him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 宋初，授武德使，出知秦州，改左飛龍使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song he was made Commissioner of Martial Virtue, sent out as prefect of Qinzhou, then changed to Commissioner of the Left Flying Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made Commissioner of Martial Virtue, sent to govern Qinzhou, then made Commissioner of the Left Flying Dragon.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，遷右領軍衛將軍，充樞密承旨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was transferred to General of the Right Army Guard and served as Secretariat liaison to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2 he became General of the Right Army Guard and Secretariat liaison to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高繼沖請命，以仁贍為荊南巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Gao Jichong submitted to the throne, Renshan was made inspector of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jichong submitted, Renshan was made inspector of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 繼沖入朝，命知軍府。

translations.literal: When Jichong came to court he was ordered to administer the military prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Jichong came to court Renshan was ordered to administer the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，遷左千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he was transferred to Grand General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande he was made Grand General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 不逾月，加內客省使。

translations.literal: Within a month he was given the additional post of Commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was also made Commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau.

sentences.zh: 二年春，召赴闕，擢為樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he was summoned to court and promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he was summoned to court and made Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 七月，加左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was given the additional rank of Grand General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was also made Grand General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 興師討蜀，命仁贍為鳳州路行營前軍都監。

translations.literal: When troops were raised to attack Shu, Renshan was made overall supervisor of the vanguard of the Fengzhou route field army.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Shu began, Renshan was made overall supervisor of the Fengzhou route vanguard.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，坐沒入生口財貨、殺降兵致蜀土擾亂，責授右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was punished for seizing captives and goods and killing surrendered soldiers, causing turmoil in Shu, and demoted to Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he was demoted to Grand General of the Right Guard for seizing captives and booty and killing surrendering troops, which threw Shu into disorder.

sentences.zh: 初，劍南之役，大將王全斌等貪財，軍政廢弛，寇盜充斥。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Jiannan campaign, the great generals Wang Quanbin and others were greedy for wealth; military discipline was lax and bandits filled the land.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in the Jiannan campaign the chief generals Wang Quanbin and others had grown greedy; discipline collapsed and bandits were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 太祖知之，每使蜀來者，令陳全斌等所入賄賂、子女及發官庫分取珠金等事，盡得其狀。

translations.literal: Taizu knew this; whenever anyone came from Shu he had them report in full on bribes Quanbin and others had taken, women they had seized, and opening the Fengde treasury to divide pearls and gold, until he had the full picture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu knew it; he had every envoy from Shu detail the bribes Quanbin and others took, the women they seized, and their opening the Fengde treasury to divide pearls and gold, until he had the full account.

sentences.zh: 及全斌等歸，帝詰仁贍，仁贍歷詆諸將過失，欲自解。

translations.literal: When Quanbin and the others returned, the emperor questioned Renshan; Renshan listed the generals' faults one by one, seeking to exculpate himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanbin and the others returned, the emperor questioned Renshan, who denounced each general's faults to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「納李廷珪妓女，開豐德庫取金寶，豈全斌輩邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You took Li Tinggui's courtesan and opened the Fengde treasury for gold and jewels—is that Quanbin and his sort?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You took Li Tinggui's courtesan and opened the Fengde treasury for gold and jewels—was that Quanbin and his men?"

sentences.zh: 仁贍不能對。

translations.literal: Renshan could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Renshan had no answer.

sentences.zh: 廷珪，故蜀將也。

translations.literal: Tinggui was a former Shu general.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui had been a Shu general.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，令送中書鞫全斌等罪，仁贍以新立功，第行降黜而已。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered Quanbin and the others sent to the Secretariat for trial; Renshan, having newly won merit, was only demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in anger sent Quanbin and the others to the Secretariat for trial; Renshan, having just earned merit, was merely demoted.

sentences.zh: 帝幸洛，以仁贍判留守司、三司兼知開封府事。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Luoyang, Renshan was made acting administrator of the Luoyang garrison, the Three Departments, and concurrently prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Luoyang, Renshan was made acting administrator of the Luoyang garrison and Three Departments and concurrently prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 及召沈倫赴行在，以仁贍為東京留守兼大內都部署。

translations.literal: When Shen Lun was summoned to the imperial camp, Renshan was made defender of the Eastern Capital and overall commander of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Lun was summoned to the imperial camp, Renshan became defender of the Eastern Capital and overall commander of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 駕還，遂判三司，俄命權宣徽北院事。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned he then administered the Three Departments and soon was ordered to act as Commissioner of the Northern Court of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned he took charge of the Three Departments and soon was ordered to act as Commissioner of the Northern Palace Secretariat court.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，拜北院使兼判如故，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was made Commissioner of the Northern Court with the same concurrent duties and given the honorary title of Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taiping Xingguo he was made Northern Court Commissioner with the same duties and honorary Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 四年，親征太原，充大內部署，仍判留守司、三司，總轄裏外巡檢司公事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the emperor's personal campaign against Taiyuan, he served as overall commander of the inner palace, still administering the garrison and Three Departments, and oversaw the inner and outer inspection offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the Taiyuan campaign, he commanded the inner palace, still ran the garrison and Three Departments, and oversaw all inspection offices.

sentences.zh: 師還，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was given the honorary title of Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was given the honorary title Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 五年，仁贍廉得近臣戚里遣人市竹木秦、隴間，聯巨筏至京師，所過關渡，矯稱制免算；

translations.literal: In the fifth year Renshan learned that close ministers and imperial kin had sent men to buy timber between Qin and Long, linking great rafts to the capital; at every pass they falsely claimed an imperial order exempting tolls;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Renshan learned that court favorites and imperial kin had men buy timber between Qin and Long, rafting it to the capital and at every pass falsely claiming imperial exemption from tolls;

sentences.zh: 既至，厚結有司，悉官市之，倍收其直。

translations.literal: once arrived they lavishly cultivated officials, who bought it all for the state at double the price.
translations.idiomatic: once it arrived they cultivated officials, who bought it all for the government at double the price.

sentences.zh: 仁贍密奏之，帝怒，以三司副使范旻、戶部判官杜載、開封府判官呂端屬吏。

translations.literal: Renshan reported this secretly; the emperor was angry and handed over the Three Departments Vice Commissioner Fan Min, Ministry of Revenue judge Du Zai, and Kaifeng judge Lü Duan to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Renshan reported secretly; the emperor in anger handed Fan Min, Du Zai, and Lü Duan over to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 旻、載具伏罔上為市竹木入官；

translations.literal: Min and Zai fully confessed to deceiving the throne by buying timber for the government;
translations.idiomatic: Min and Zai confessed to deceiving the throne by procuring timber for the government;

sentences.zh: 端為秦府親吏喬璉請託執事者。

translations.literal: Duan had interceded for Qiao Lian, a personal clerk of the Prince of Qin, with those in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Duan had lobbied for Qiao Lian, a personal clerk of the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 貶旻為房州司戶，載均州司戶，端商州司戶。

translations.literal: Min was demoted to registrar of Fangzhou, Zai to registrar of Junzhou, and Duan to registrar of Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Min was demoted to registrar of Fangzhou, Zai of Junzhou, and Duan of Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 判四方館事程德玄、武德使劉知信，翰林使杜彥圭，日騎、天武四廂都指揮使趙延溥，武德副使竇神興，左衛上將軍張永德，左領軍衛上將軍祁廷訓，駙馬都尉王承衎、石保吉、魏咸信，並坐販竹木入官，責降罰奉。

translations.literal: Cheng Dexuan, Commissioner of the Four Directions Hostel; Liu Zhixin, Commissioner of Martial Virtue; Du Yangui, Hanlin Commissioner; Zhao Yanpu, overall commander of the Sun and Heavenly Martial guards; Dou Shenxing, Vice Commissioner of Martial Virtue; Zhang Yongde, Grand General of the Left Guard; Qi Tingxun, Grand General of the Left Army Guard; and the imperial sons-in-law Wang Chengyan, Shi Baoji, and Wei Xianxin—all were punished for selling timber to the government and had their salaries reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Dexuan, Liu Zhixin, Du Yangui, Zhao Yanpu, Dou Shenxing, Zhang Yongde, Qi Tingxun, and the imperial sons-in-law Wang Chengyan, Shi Baoji, and Wei Xianxin were all punished for selling timber to the government and had their salaries cut.

sentences.zh: 是歲，車駕北巡，命仁贍為大內部署。

translations.literal: That year, when the imperial carriage toured the north, Renshan was made overall commander of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: That year, on the northern tour, Renshan was made overall commander of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 七年春，以政事與僚屬相矛盾，爭辯帝前，仁贍辭屈，責授右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, because of policy disputes with his subordinates he argued before the emperor; Renshan was speechless and demoted to Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he quarreled with subordinates before the emperor; Renshan was silenced and demoted to Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 翌日，改唐州防禦使，月給奉錢三十萬。

translations.literal: The next day he was changed to Defender of Tang Prefecture with a monthly salary of three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was made Defender of Tang Prefecture with a monthly salary of three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 仁贍之獲罪也，兵部郎中、判勾院宋琪及三司判官並降秩。

translations.literal: When Renshan was punished, Song Qi, Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and judge of the Audit Office, and the Three Departments judges were all reduced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Renshan fell, Song Qi and the Three Departments judges were all demoted.

sentences.zh: 先是，仁贍掌計司殆十年，恣下吏為奸，怙恩寵無敢發者；

translations.literal: Earlier, Renshan had run the revenue office for nearly ten years, letting subordinates commit fraud while relying on favor—none dared expose him;
translations.idiomatic: Renshan had run the revenue office nearly ten years, letting subordinates cheat while his favor protected him;

sentences.zh: 前者發范旻等事，中外益畏其口。

translations.literal: after he exposed Fan Min and the others, court and country alike feared his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: after he exposed Fan Min and the others, everyone feared his accusations.

sentences.zh: 會屬吏陳恕等數人率以皦察不畏強禦自任，因議本司事有不協者。

translations.literal: Several subordinates led by Chen Shu took it on themselves to be sharp-eyed and unafraid of the powerful, and debated matters in the office on which they did not agree.
