translations.idiomatic: Subordinates led by Chen Shu styled themselves incorruptible and fearless, and disputed office policy.

sentences.zh: 朝參日，恕獨出班持狀奏其事。

translations.literal: On a day of court audience Shu alone stepped from the ranks holding a memorial and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At court Shu alone stepped forward with a memorial reporting the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝詰之，仁贍屈伏。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned him; Renshan confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him; Renshan admitted guilt.

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，故及於譴，而恕等悉獎擢。

translations.literal: The emperor was very angry and so punished him, while Shu and the others were all rewarded and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and punished Renshan, while Shu and the others were all promoted.

sentences.zh: 琪與恕等聯事，始合謀同奏，至帝前而宋琪猶附會仁贍，故亦左降。

translations.literal: Qi had acted with Shu and the others; at first they plotted to report together, but before the emperor Qi still sided with Renshan, and so he too was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had plotted with Shu to report together, but at court he still sided with Renshan and was demoted too.

sentences.zh: 仁贍既失權勢，因怏怏成疾，數日卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: Once Renshan had lost power he fell ill from resentment and died within days, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of power, he fell ill from resentment and died within days at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 後帝因言及三司財賦，謂宰相趙普等曰：「王仁贍領邦計積年，恣吏為奸，諸場院官皆隱沒官錢以千萬計，朕悉令罷之，命使分掌。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor spoke of Three Departments finances, he told the chief councilor Zhao Pu and others: "Wang Renshan ran state revenue for years and let clerks commit fraud; officials at every depot hid government money by the tens of millions—I have abolished them all and sent commissioners to take charge separately.
translations.idiomatic: Later, discussing Three Departments revenue, the emperor told Zhao Pu and others, "Wang Renshan ran state finances for years while clerks cheated; depot officials hid tens of millions—I abolished them and sent commissioners to take charge.

sentences.zh: 仁贍再三言，恐虧舊數，朕拒之。

translations.literal: Renshan repeatedly said he feared the old totals would suffer; I refused.
translations.idiomatic: Renshan kept saying the old totals would suffer; I refused.

sentences.zh: 未逾年，舊獲千緡者為一二萬緡，萬緡者為六七萬緡，其利數倍，用度既足，儻遇水旱，即可免民租稅。

translations.literal: Within a year what had yielded a thousand strings yielded ten or twenty thousand, and what had yielded ten thousand yielded sixty or seventy thousand; profits multiplied several times; expenses were met, and if flood or drought came, the people's taxes could be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year a thousand-string yield became ten or twenty thousand, and ten thousand became sixty or seventy thousand; profits multiplied; expenses were met, and in flood or drought taxes could be remitted.

sentences.zh: 仁贍心知其非，頗亦慚悸，朕優容之。」

translations.literal: Renshan knew in his heart he had been wrong and was quite ashamed and fearful; I treated him leniently."
translations.idiomatic: Renshan knew he was wrong and was ashamed; I treated him leniently."

sentences.zh: 子昭雍，為崇儀副使。

translations.literal: His son Zhaoyong was Deputy Commissioner of the Honored Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaoyong was Deputy Commissioner of Honored Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 楚昭輔

translations.literal: Chu Zhaofu
translations.idiomatic: Chu Zhaofu

sentences.zh: 楚昭輔，字拱辰，宋州宋城人。

translations.literal: Chu Zhaofu, styled Gongchen, was a native of Songcheng in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Zhaofu, styled Gongchen, was from Songcheng in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少事華帥劉詞。

translations.literal: In youth he served the Huazhou commander Liu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served Huazhou commander Liu Ci.

sentences.zh: 詞卒，事太祖，隸麾下，以才幹稱，甚信任之。

translations.literal: When Ci died he served Taizu, attached to his command, and was famed for ability; Taizu trusted him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci died he entered Taizu's service, famed for ability and deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 陳橋師還，昭憲太后在城中，太祖憂之，遣昭輔問起居，昭輔具言士眾推戴之狀，太后乃安。

translations.literal: When the Chenqiao army returned, Empress Dowager Zhaoxian was still in the city; Taizu was anxious and sent Zhaofu to inquire after her; Zhaofu fully reported how the troops had acclaimed him, and the empress dowager was reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chenqiao army returned, Empress Dowager Zhaoxian was in the city; Taizu sent Zhaofu to inquire; he reported the troops' acclamation fully, and she was reassured.

sentences.zh: 宋初，為軍器庫使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song he was Commissioner of the Armory.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was Commissioner of the Armory.

sentences.zh: 太祖親討澤、潞，及征淮揚，並以昭輔為京城巡檢。

translations.literal: When Taizu personally attacked Ze and Lu and campaigned on the Huai and Yang, Zhaofu was each time made inspector of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizu's campaigns against Ze and Lu and on the Huai and Yang, Zhaofu was each time made capital inspector.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，權知揚州，使江表。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong he was acting prefect of Yangzhou and sent to the south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 4 he was acting prefect of Yangzhou and sent to the Jiangnan region.

sentences.zh: 還，命鉤校左藏庫金帛，數日而畢，條對稱旨。

translations.literal: On his return he was ordered to audit gold and silks in the Left Treasury; he finished in days and his itemized report pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On return he audited the Left Treasury's gold and silks, finished in days, and his report pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，帝以其能心計，拜左驍衛大將軍、權判三司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao the emperor, because of his skill in accounting, made him Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry and acting administrator of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 4, for his accounting skill, he was made Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry and acting administrator of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，命權宣徽南院事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered to act as Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was ordered to act as Commissioner of the Southern Palace Secretariat court.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，拜樞密使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was made Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taiping Xingguo he was made Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the honorary title of Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was given the honorary title Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: On the Taiyuan campaign he was given the honorary title of Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On the Taiyuan campaign he was given the honorary title Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 俄以足疾請告，帝親臨問。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of foot ailment he requested leave; the emperor personally visited to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took leave for foot ailment; the emperor visited him in person.

sentences.zh: 以所居湫隘，命有司廣之，昭輔慮侵民地，固讓不願治。

translations.literal: Because his residence was cramped, the emperor ordered the authorities to enlarge it; Zhaofu feared encroaching on commoners' land and firmly declined to have it done.
translations.idiomatic: His house being cramped, the emperor ordered it enlarged; Zhaofu feared encroaching on neighbors' land and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其意，賜白金萬兩，令別市第。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his intent and gave him ten thousand taels of white silver, ordering him to buy another residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, gave ten thousand taels of silver, and told him to buy another house.

sentences.zh: 昭輔被疾，家居近一歲，始以石熙載代之。

translations.literal: Zhaofu was ill and stayed home nearly a year before Shi Xizai replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he stayed home nearly a year before Shi Xizai replaced him.

sentences.zh: 昭輔不求解職，上亦不忍罷。

translations.literal: Zhaofu did not seek to resign; the emperor also could not bear to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaofu did not ask to resign; the emperor could not bear to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 會郊祀畢，罷為驍騎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When the suburban sacrifice was completed he was dismissed as Grand General of the Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban sacrifice he was dismissed as Grand General of the Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: After a year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈侍中，命中使護其喪歸葬鄉里。

translations.literal: Court was suspended; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant; an imperial envoy was ordered to escort the funeral home for burial in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant; an envoy escorted his body home for burial.

sentences.zh: 無子，錄其兄子吉為供奉官，敏為殿直。

translations.literal: He had no son; his elder brother's sons Ji and Min were recorded as Honored Attendant and Palace Attendant respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, his nephews Ji and Min were appointed Honored Attendant and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 昭輔性勤介，人不敢干以私，然頗吝嗇，前後賜予萬計，悉聚而畜之。

translations.literal: Zhaofu was diligent and upright; no one dared approach him with private requests, yet he was quite stingy; gifts numbering in the tens of thousands he gathered and hoarded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaofu was diligent and upright; none dared seek private favors, yet he was stingy and hoarded gifts by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 嘗引賓客故舊至藏中縱觀，且曰：「吾無汗馬勞，徒以際會得此，吾為國家守爾，後當獻於上。」

translations.literal: He once led guests and old friends to view his treasury and said: "I have no sweat-and-horse toil but gained this by chance; I hold it for the state and will later present it to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: He once showed guests his treasury and said, "I earned no battlefield merit but gained this by fortune; I hold it for the state and will present it to the throne."

sentences.zh: 及罷機務，悉以市善田宅，時論鄙之。

translations.literal: When he left high office he used it all to buy good fields and houses; public opinion despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office he spent it all on land and houses; opinion despised him.

sentences.zh: 初，詞卒，昭輔來京師，問卜於瞽者劉悟。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ci died, Zhaofu came to the capital and asked the blind diviner Liu Wu for a reading.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci died, Zhaofu came to the capital and consulted the blind diviner Liu Wu.

sentences.zh: 悟為筮卜，曰：「汝遇貴人，見奇表豐下者即汝主也，宜謹事之，汝當貴矣。」

translations.literal: Wu performed divination and said: "You will meet a noble man; when you see one of strange appearance and full lower face, that is your lord—serve him carefully and you will rise."
translations.idiomatic: Wu divined and said, "You will meet a noble; when you see a man of strange bearing and full lower face, that is your lord—serve him well and you will rise."

sentences.zh: 及見太祖，狀貌如悟言，遂委質焉。

translations.literal: When he saw Taizu, his appearance matched Wu's words, and he thereupon offered his service.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Taizu, the man's appearance matched Wu's prophecy, and he entered his service.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，錄弟之子諒為借職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping his younger brother's son Liang was recorded as borrowed office.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3 his nephew Liang was given borrowed office rank.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年，又錄從孫鼎為右班殿直。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his collateral descendant Ding was again recorded as Right Class Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 8 his collateral descendant Ding was made Right Class Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 吉至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Ji reached Inner Hall Honored Class.
translations.idiomatic: Ji rose to Inner Hall Honored Class.

sentences.zh: 吉子隨，敏子咸，並進士及第，隨為太常博士，咸屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: Ji's son Sui and Min's son Xian both passed the civil service examination; Sui was Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Xian Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Sui and Min's son Xian both passed the jinshi; Sui became Doctor of Imperial Sacrifices, Xian Vice Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 李處耘

translations.literal: Li Chuyun
translations.idiomatic: Li Chuyun

sentences.zh: 李處耘，潞州上黨人。

translations.literal: Li Chuyun was a native of Shangdang in Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chuyun was from Shangdang in Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父肇，仕後唐，歷軍校，至檢校司徒。

translations.literal: His father Zhao served the Later Tang, rising through army posts to Honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao served Later Tang, rising through military ranks to Honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 從討王都定州，契丹來援，唐師不利，肇力戰死之。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Wang Du at Dingzhou the Khitan came to aid him; the Tang army fared badly and Zhao died fighting fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Wang Du at Dingzhou the Khitan intervened; the Tang army suffered and Zhao died in fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 晉末，處耘尚幼，隨兄處疇至京師，遇張彥澤斬關而入，縱士卒剽略。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin, Chuyun was still young; he followed his elder brother Chuchou to the capital and encountered Zhang Yanzhe breaking through the gate, letting soldiers plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jin, Chuyun was young; he followed his brother Chuchou to the capital when Zhang Yanzhe broke in and let troops loot.

sentences.zh: 處耘年猶未冠，獨當里門，射殺十數人，眾無敢當者。

translations.literal: Chuyun was not yet capped; alone he held the lane gate and shot down more than ten men; none dared face him.
translations.idiomatic: Not yet of age, he alone held the lane gate and killed more than ten men; none dared approach.

sentences.zh: 會暮夜，遂退。

translations.literal: Night fell and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At nightfall they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 迨曉復鬥，又殺數人，鬥未解。

translations.literal: At dawn they fought again; he killed several more before the fight was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn fighting resumed; he killed several more before it ended.

sentences.zh: 有所親握兵，聞難來赴，遂得釋，里中賴之。

translations.literal: A kinsman who held troops, hearing of the danger, came to the rescue; he was released, and the neighborhood relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman with troops heard and came; he was saved, and the neighborhood owed him.

sentences.zh: 漢初，折從阮帥府州，召置門下，委以軍務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Zhe Congruan commanded Fuzhou and took him into his staff, entrusting him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Han, Zhe Congruan of Fuzhou took him on staff and entrusted him with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 從阮後歷鄧、滑、陝、邠四節度，處耘皆從之。

translations.literal: Congruan later held the four commands of Deng, Hua, Shaan, and Bin; Chuyun followed him throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Congruan later held Deng, Hua, Shaan, and Bin; Chuyun followed him to each.

sentences.zh: 在新平日，折氏甥詣闕誣告處耘之罪，周祖信之，黜為宜祿鎮將。

translations.literal: At Xinping, a nephew of the Zhe clan went to court to accuse Chuyun falsely; Zhou Taizu believed it and demoted him to garrison commander of Yilu.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinping a Zhe nephew falsely accused him at court; Zhou Taizu believed it and demoted him to garrison commander of Yilu.

sentences.zh: 從阮表雪其冤，詔復隸麾下。

translations.literal: Congruan memorialized to clear his name; an edict restored him to Congruan's command.
translations.idiomatic: Congruan memorialized to clear him; an edict restored him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，從阮遺表稱處耘可用，會李繼勳鎮河陽，詔署以右職。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era Congruan's deathbed memorial praised Chuyun's ability; when Li Jixun took Henei, an edict appointed him to a senior military post.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiande, Congruan's deathbed memorial praised him; when Li Jixun took Henei, an edict gave him a senior military post.

sentences.zh: 繼勳初不為禮，因會將吏宴射，處耘連四發中的，繼勳大奇之，令升堂拜母，稍委郡務，俾掌河津。

translations.literal: Jixun at first showed him no courtesy; at a feast with officers shooting, Chuyun hit the target four times in succession; Jixun was greatly impressed and had him enter the hall to bow to his mother, gradually entrusted him with prefectural affairs, and put him in charge of the river crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun at first slighted him; at an officers' archery feast Chuyun hit four targets in a row; Jixun was amazed, had him bow to his mother, and gradually entrusted him with prefectural affairs and the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 處耘白繼勳曰：「此津往來者懼有奸焉，不可不察也。」

translations.literal: Chuyun told Jixun: "Travelers at this crossing may hide spies—it cannot go unexamined."
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun told Jixun, "Traffic at this crossing may hide spies—it must be watched."

sentences.zh: 居數月，果得契丹諜者，索之，有與西川、江南蠟書，即遣處耘部送闕下。

translations.literal: After several months he indeed seized a Khitan spy; searched, he had wax letters to Western Shu and Jiangnan, and Chuyun was sent to escort him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he seized a Khitan spy with wax letters to Western Shu and Jiangnan and escorted him to court.

sentences.zh: 太祖時領殿前親軍，繼勳罷鎮，世宗以處耘隸太祖帳下，補都押衙。

translations.literal: When Taizu then commanded the Palace Front guard, Jixun left his post, and Shizong assigned Chuyun to Taizu's command as chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu commanded the Palace Front, Jixun left his post and Shizong assigned Chuyun to Taizu as chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 會太祖出征，駐軍陳橋，處耘見軍中謀欲推戴，遽白太宗，與王彥升謀，召馬仁瑀、李漢超等定議，始入白太祖，太祖拒之。

translations.literal: When Taizu marched out and the army halted at Chenqiao, Chuyun saw the troops plotting acclamation, hurriedly informed the Prince of Jin, and with Wang Yansheng plotted to summon Ma Renyu and Li Hanchao to settle the plan; they first entered to tell Taizu, who refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu camped at Chenqiao, Chuyun saw the troops plotting acclamation, told the Prince of Jin, and with Wang Yansheng summoned Ma Renyu and Li Hanchao; they told Taizu first, who refused.

sentences.zh: 俄而諸軍大噪，入驛門，太祖不能卻。

translations.literal: Soon the whole army roared and entered the post station; Taizu could not turn them back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the whole army roared into the post station; Taizu could not hold them back.

sentences.zh: 處耘臨機決事，謀無不中，太祖嘉之，授客省使兼樞密承旨、右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Chuyun decided affairs on the spot; none of his plans failed; Taizu praised him and appointed him Commissioner of the Guest Bureau, concurrent Secretariat liaison to Military Affairs, and General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun decided on the spot; his plans never failed; Taizu praised him and made him Commissioner of the Guest Bureau, Military Affairs liaison, and General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 從平澤、潞，遷羽林大將軍、宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: On the pacification of Ze and Lu he was transferred to Grand General of the Forest Guard and Commissioner of the Northern Palace Secretariat court.
translations.idiomatic: After Ze and Lu were pacified he became Grand General of the Forest Guard and Northern Court Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 討李重進，為行營兵馬都監。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Li Chongjin he was overall military supervisor of the field army.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Li Chongjin he was overall military supervisor of the field army.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以處耘知揚州。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified Chuyun was made prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were crushed he was made prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 大兵之後，境內凋弊，處耘勤於綏撫，奏減城中居民屋稅，民皆悅服。

translations.literal: After the great armies, the territory was devastated; Chuyun worked hard at relief and memorialized to reduce house taxes in the city; the people were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: After the armies the region was ruined; Chuyun worked hard at relief, cut city house taxes, and won the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，詔歸京師，老幼遮道涕泣，累日不得去。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong an edict recalled him to the capital; old and young blocked the road weeping; for days he could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 3 he was recalled; old and young blocked the road weeping for days.

sentences.zh: 拜宣徽南院使兼樞密副使，賜甲第一區。

translations.literal: He was made Commissioner of the Southern Court and Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs and given one set of armor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Southern Court Commissioner and Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs and given a suit of armor.

sentences.zh: 朗州軍亂，詔慕容延釗率師討之，以處耘為都監。

translations.literal: When Langzhou's army rebelled, Murong Yanzhao was ordered to lead troops against it and Chuyun was made overall supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Langzhou rebelled, Murong Yanzhao was ordered to attack and Chuyun was overall supervisor.

sentences.zh: 入辭，帝親授方略，令會兵漢上。

translations.literal: On entering audience the emperor personally gave strategy and ordered him to join forces on the Han.
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor personally gave strategy and ordered him to join forces on the Han.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷遣內酒坊副使盧懷忠使荊南，覘勢強弱。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had sent Lu Huaizhong, Vice Commissioner of the Inner Wine Bureau, to Jingnan to observe strength and weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had sent Lu Huaizhong to Jingnan to gauge strength.

sentences.zh: 使還，具言可取之狀，遂命處耘圖之。

translations.literal: On his return he fully reported that it could be taken, and Chuyun was ordered to plan it.
translations.idiomatic: He returned reporting it could be taken, and Chuyun was ordered to plan the conquest.

sentences.zh: 處耘至襄州，先遣閤門使丁德裕假道荊南，請具薪水給軍，荊人辭以民庶恐懼，願供芻餼於百里外。

translations.literal: Chuyun reached Xiangzhou and first sent the Gate Commissioner Ding Deyu to ask passage through Jingnan and request fodder and supplies for the army; the Jing people pleaded that the people feared and wished to supply fodder a hundred li outside.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangzhou he sent Ding Deyu to ask passage through Jingnan for supplies; the Jing people asked to supply fodder a hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 處耘又遣德裕諭之，乃聽命。

translations.literal: Chuyun again sent Deyu to instruct them, and they obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun sent Deyu again and they obeyed.

sentences.zh: 遂令軍中曰：「入江陵城有不由路及擅入民舍者斬。」

translations.literal: He then ordered the army: "Whoever enters Jiangling city not by the road or enters private houses without permission will be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the army: anyone entering Jiangling off the route or private houses would be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 師次荊門，高繼沖遣其叔保寅及軍校梁延嗣奉牛酒犒師，且來覘也。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jingmen; Gao Jichong sent his uncle Baoyin and officer Liang Yansi with cattle and wine to reward the army and also to spy.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingmen, Gao Jichong sent his uncle Baoyin and officer Liang Yansi with cattle and wine to reward the army and spy.

sentences.zh: 處耘待之有加，諭令翌日先還。

translations.literal: Chuyun treated them generously and told them to return the next day first.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun treated them well and told them to return first the next day.

sentences.zh: 延嗣大喜，令報繼沖以無虞。

translations.literal: Yansi was delighted and had them report to Jichong that there was no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yansi was delighted and told Jichong there was no danger.

sentences.zh: 荊門距江陵百餘里，是夕，召保寅等飲宴延釗之帳。

translations.literal: Jingmen was over a hundred li from Jiangling; that evening he summoned Baoyin and the others to drink in Yanzhao's tent.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmen was over a hundred li from Jiangling; that evening he feasted Baoyin in Yanzhao's tent.

sentences.zh: 處耘密遣輕騎數千倍道前進。

translations.literal: Chuyun secretly sent several thousand light cavalry by a forced march ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun secretly sent thousands of light cavalry ahead by forced march.

sentences.zh: 繼沖但俟保寅、延嗣之還，遽聞大軍奄至，即惶怖出迎，遇處耘於江陵北十五里。

translations.literal: Jichong only waited for Baoyin and Yansi to return when he suddenly heard the great army had arrived; in terror he went out to meet them and encountered Chuyun fifteen li north of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Jichong waited for Baoyin and Yansi; suddenly the main army was upon him; terrified, he met Chuyun fifteen li north of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 處耘揖繼沖，令待延釗，遂率親兵先入登北門。

translations.literal: Chuyun bowed to Jichong and told him to wait for Yanzhao, then led his personal troops in first and ascended the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun bowed to Jichong, told him to wait for Yanzhao, and led his guard in through the north gate.

sentences.zh: 比繼沖還，則兵已分據城中，荊人束手聽命。

translations.literal: By the time Jichong returned, troops already held the city; the Jing people submitted with hands bound.
translations.idiomatic: When Jichong returned, troops held the city; the Jing people submitted.

sentences.zh: 即調發江陵卒萬餘人，並其師，晨夜趨朗州。

translations.literal: He immediately mobilized more than ten thousand Jiangling troops with his own army and hurried day and night toward Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized ten thousand Jiangling troops with his army and hurried to Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 又先遣別將分麾下及江陵兵趨岳州，大破賊於三江口，獲船七百餘艘，斬首四千級。

translations.literal: He had also sent separate generals with his own troops and Jiangling troops toward Yuezhou; they routed the rebels at Sanjiangkou, took more than seven hundred boats, and beheaded four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Separate columns went to Yuezhou, routed rebels at Sanjiangkou, took seven hundred boats, and beheaded four thousand.

sentences.zh: 又遇賊帥張從富於澧江，擊敗之。

translations.literal: They again met the rebel chief Zhang Congfu on the Li River and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: They met rebel chief Zhang Congfu on the Li River and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 逐北至敖山砦，賊棄砦走，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Pursuing north to Aoshan stockade, the rebels abandoned it and fled; captives were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to Aoshan, the rebels fled; captives were many.

sentences.zh: 處耘釋所俘體肥者數十人，令左右分啖之，黥其少健者，令先入朗州。

translations.literal: Chuyun released several dozen fat captives and had his attendants eat them in portions, tattooed the younger strong ones, and had them enter Langzhou first.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun released fat captives for his men to eat in portions, tattooed the young and strong, and sent them into Langzhou first.

sentences.zh: 會暮，宿砦中，遲明，延釗大軍繼至。

translations.literal: At dusk they camped in the stockade; at dawn Yanzhao's main army followed.
translations.idiomatic: They camped at dusk; at dawn Yanzhao's main army arrived.

sentences.zh: 黥者先入城言，被擒者悉為大軍所啖，朗人大懼，縱火焚城而潰。

translations.literal: The tattooed men entered the city first saying all captives had been eaten by the great army; the Lang people were greatly afraid, set fires, burned the city, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The tattooed men entered saying captives were eaten by the army; Langzhou panicked, burned the city, and fled.

sentences.zh: 會朗帥周保權年尚幼，為大將汪端劫匿於江南砦僧寺中。

translations.literal: The Lang commander Zhou Baoquan was still young and had been seized by the great general Wang Duan and hidden in a Jiangnan stockade monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Lang commander Zhou Baoquan was young; the general Wang Duan had seized him and hidden him in a Jiangnan monastery.

sentences.zh: 處耘遣麾下將田守奇帥師渡江獲之。

translations.literal: Chuyun sent his officer Tian Shouqi to lead troops across the river and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun sent Tian Shouqi across the river to capture him.

sentences.zh: 遂入潭州，盡得荊湖之地。

translations.literal: He then entered Tanzhou and fully gained the Jinghu region.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Tanzhou and secured the entire Jinghu region.

sentences.zh: 初，師至襄州，衢肆鬻餅者率減少，倍取軍人之直。

translations.literal: When the army first reached Xiangzhou, cake sellers in the market generally gave less and charged the soldiers double.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangzhou, cake sellers shorted portions and doubled prices for soldiers.

sentences.zh: 處耘捕得其尤者二人送延釗，延釗怒不受，往復三四，處耘遂命斬於市以徇。

translations.literal: Chuyun seized the worst offenders and sent them to Yanzhao; Yanzhao angrily would not accept them; back and forth three or four times; Chuyun then ordered them beheaded in the market as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun seized the worst offenders and sent them to Yanzhao, who refused them; after several exchanges Chuyun had them beheaded in the market.

sentences.zh: 延釗所部小校司義舍於荊州客將王氏家，使酒凶恣，王氏愬於處耘。

translations.literal: A petty officer of Yanzhao's command named Si Yi lodged at the Jingzhou host Wang's house, sent for wine and acted violently; Wang complained to Chuyun.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao's petty officer Si Yi lodged with a Jingzhou host, got drunk and violent; the host complained to Chuyun.

sentences.zh: 處耘召義嗬責，義又譖處耘於延釗。

translations.literal: Chuyun summoned Yi and berated him; Yi also slandered Chuyun to Yanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun berated Yi; Yi slandered Chuyun to Yanzhao.

sentences.zh: 至白湖，處耘望見軍人入民舍，良久，舍中人大呼求救，遣捕之，即延釗圉人也，乃鞭其背，延釗怒斬之。

translations.literal: At Baihu Lake Chuyun saw soldiers enter a commoner's house; after a long while someone inside cried for help; he sent to seize them—it was Yanzhao's groom—and flogged his back; Yanzhao in anger beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: At Baihu Lake Chuyun saw soldiers enter a house; cries for help came; he seized Yanzhao's groom and flogged him; Yanzhao angrily beheaded the groom.

sentences.zh: 由是大不協，更相論奏。

translations.literal: From this they were greatly at odds and each memorialized against the other.
translations.idiomatic: They fell out badly and each reported the other.

sentences.zh: 朝議以延釗宿將貰其過，謫處耘為淄州刺史。

translations.literal: Court opinion, because Yanzhao was a veteran general, forgave his fault and demoted Chuyun to prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion favored the veteran Yanzhao; Chuyun was demoted to prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 處耘懼，不敢自明。

translations.literal: Chuyun was afraid and did not dare clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun was afraid and did not defend himself.

sentences.zh: 在州數年，乾德四年，卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: After several years in the prefecture, in the fourth year of Qiande he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office, in Qiande 4 he died at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈宣德軍節度、檢校太傅，賜地葬於洛陽偏橋村。

translations.literal: Court was suspended; he was posthumously made military commissioner of the Xunde army and Honorary Grand Tutor, with land granted for burial at Pianqiao village in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended; he was posthumously made Xunde military commissioner and Honorary Grand Tutor, with burial land at Pianqiao near Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 處耘有度量，善談當世之務，居常以功名為己任。

translations.literal: Chuyun had breadth of mind and was skilled at discussing affairs of the age; in daily life he took merit and fame as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun was magnanimous and skilled at current affairs; he lived for merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 荊湖之役，處耘以近臣護軍，自以受太祖之遇，思有以報，故臨事專制，不顧群議，遂至於貶。

translations.literal: In the Jinghu campaign Chuyun, as a close minister overseeing the army, felt he owed Taizu for his favor and wished to repay it; therefore in action he acted on his own authority, heedless of collective opinion, and so was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghu, as a favored minister overseeing troops, he repaid Taizu's trust with arbitrary command and was demoted.

sentences.zh: 後太祖頗追念之。

translations.literal: Later Taizu often recalled him with regret.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizu often recalled him with regret.

sentences.zh: 及開寶中，為太宗納其次女為妃，即明德皇后也。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao era the Prince of Jin took his second daughter as consort—she became Empress Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao the Prince of Jin married his second daughter—the future Empress Mingde.

sentences.zh: 子繼隆、繼和，自有傳；

translations.literal: His sons Jilong and Jihe have their own biographies;
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jilong and Jihe have separate biographies;

sentences.zh: 繼恂，官至洛苑使、順州刺史，贈左神武大將軍。

translations.literal: Jixun reached Commissioner of the Luoyuan and prefect of Shunzhou and was posthumously made Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun became Luoyuan Commissioner and prefect of Shunzhou, posthumously Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 繼恂子昭遜，為供備庫使。

translations.literal: Jixun's son Zhaoxun was Commissioner of the Supply Preparation Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun's son Zhaoxun was Supply Preparation Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 處疇，官至作坊使，子繼凝。

translations.literal: Chuchou reached Commissioner of the Workshops; his son Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Chuchou became Workshops Commissioner; his son Jining.

sentences.zh: 子 繼隆

translations.literal: Son Jilong
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jilong

sentences.zh: 繼隆，字霸圖，幼養於伯父處疇。

translations.literal: Jilong, styled Batu, was raised in youth by his uncle Chuchou.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong, styled Batu, was raised by his uncle Chuchou.

sentences.zh: 及長，以父蔭補供奉官。

translations.literal: When grown, through his father's privilege he was appointed Honored Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he entered office through his father's privilege as Honored Attendant.

sentences.zh: 處耘貶淄州，繼隆亦除籍。

translations.literal: When Chuyun was demoted to Zizhou, Jilong was also struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuyun was demoted to Zizhou, Jilong was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 會長春節，與其母入貢，復舊官。

translations.literal: At the Long Spring festival he came to court with his mother to present tribute and was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: At the Long Spring festival he came to court with his mother and was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 時權臣與處耘有宿憾者，忌繼隆有才，繼隆因落魄不治產，以遊獵為娛。

translations.literal: At the time a powerful minister bore old hatred toward Chuyun and feared Jilong's talent; Jilong therefore lived in neglect without managing property, taking hunting for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful minister hated Chuyun and feared Jilong's talent; Jilong lived idly, hunting for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 乾德中平蜀，選為果、閬監軍，年方弱冠，母憂其未更事，將輔以處耘左右。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified in Qiande he was chosen as overseer of Guo and Lang; he was barely twenty, and his mother worried he lacked experience and wished to send Chuyun's old attendants to assist.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified in Qiande he was chosen overseer of Guo and Lang; barely twenty, his mother wished to send old attendants.

sentences.zh: 繼隆曰：「是行兒自有立，豈須此輩，願不以為慮。」

translations.literal: Jilong said: "On this journey your son will make his own mark—why need these people? Do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Jilong said, "On this trip I will prove myself—no need for them; do not worry."

sentences.zh: 母慰而遣之。

translations.literal: His mother was comforted and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was reassured and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 代還，夜涉棧道，雨滑，與馬偕墜絕澗，深十餘丈，絓於大樹。

translations.literal: On returning from replacement of duty, at night he crossed a plank road; rain made it slippery and he fell with his horse into a ravine more than ten zhang deep, caught on a great tree.
translations.idiomatic: Returning at night on a plank road, rain made it slippery; he and his horse fell into a ravine over ten zhang deep and caught on a tree.

sentences.zh: 騎卒馳數十里外，取火引綆以出之。

translations.literal: Riders galloped several tens of li for fire and rope to pull him out.
translations.idiomatic: Riders rode tens of li for fire and rope to haul him out.

sentences.zh: 會征江南，領雄武卒三百戍邵州，止給刀盾。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Jiangnan began he led three hundred Valiant Martial troops to garrison Shaozhou, given only shields and blades.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jiangnan campaign he led three hundred Valiant Martial troops to garrison Shaozhou with only shields and blades.

sentences.zh: 蠻賊數千陣長沙南，截其道。

translations.literal: Several thousand barbarian bandits arrayed south of Changsha and blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand barbarian bandits blocked the road south of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 繼隆率眾力戰，賊遁去，手足俱中毒矢，得良藥而愈，部卒死傷者三之一。

translations.literal: Jilong led his men in fierce fighting; the bandits fled; his hands and feet were all struck by poisoned arrows but good medicine cured him; a third of his troops were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong fought fiercely; the bandits fled; poisoned arrows struck his hands and feet but he recovered; a third of his men were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其勇敢而器重之。

translations.literal: Taizu heard of his bravery and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu heard of his bravery and valued him.

sentences.zh: 又與石曦率兵襲袁州，破桃田砦，追賊二十里，入潭富砦，焚其梯衝芻積。

translations.literal: He also with Shi Xi led troops to raid Yuanzhou, broke Taotian stockade, pursued the enemy twenty li, entered Tanfu stockade, and burned ladders, rams, and fodder stores.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Xi he raided Yuanzhou, broke Taotian stockade, pursued twenty li, burned siege equipment at Tanfu.

sentences.zh: 復從李符督荊湖漕運，給征南諸軍。

translations.literal: He again followed Li Fu in supervising Jinghu transport to supply the southern campaign armies.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Li Fu supervising Jinghu transport for the southern armies.

sentences.zh: 吳人以王師不便水戰，多出舟師斷餉道，繼隆屢與鬥，糧悉善達。

translations.literal: The Wu, thinking the Song army unfit for water warfare, often sent fleets to cut the supply route; Jilong fought them repeatedly and grain all arrived safely.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu, thinking Song troops poor at sea, cut supply lines; Jilong fought them repeatedly and grain arrived safely.

sentences.zh: 日馳四五百里，常令往來覘候。

translations.literal: He rode four or five hundred li a day and was often ordered to scout back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: He rode four or five hundred li a day on scouting missions.

sentences.zh: 一日中途遇虎，射殺之。

translations.literal: One day en route he met a tiger and shot it dead.
translations.idiomatic: One day he met a tiger on the road and shot it dead.

sentences.zh: 嘗獲吳將，部送赴闕，至項縣而病，斬其首以獻，太祖益嘉之。

translations.literal: He once captured a Wu general and escorted him to court; at Xiang county he fell ill and beheaded him to present; Taizu praised him the more.
translations.idiomatic: He captured a Wu general; at Xiang county the man fell ill and he beheaded him for presentation; Taizu praised him further.

sentences.zh: 與吳人戰，流矢中額，以所冠胄堅厚，得不傷。

translations.literal: In fighting the Wu a stray arrow struck his forehead; because his helmet was thick and strong he was not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow struck his forehead; his thick helmet saved him.

sentences.zh: 太祖察其才，且追念其父，欲拔用之，謂曰：「昇州平，可持捷書來，當厚賞汝。」

translations.literal: Taizu saw his talent and, recalling his father, wished to promote him and said: "When Shengzhou falls, bring the victory report and I will richly reward you."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, recalling his father, said, "When Shengzhou falls, bring the victory report and I will richly reward you."

sentences.zh: 時內侍使軍中者十數輩，皆伺城陷獻捷，會有機事當入奏，皆不願行，而繼隆獨請赴闕。

translations.literal: At the time several dozen inner attendants in the army all waited for the city to fall to present victory; when urgent business required someone to enter court, none wished to go, but Jilong alone asked to go to court.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of inner attendants waited to present victory when the city fell; when court business arose none would go, but Jilong alone volunteered.

sentences.zh: 太宗見其來，時城尚未下，甚訝之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin saw him come, the city was not yet down, and he was greatly surprised.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin was greatly surprised to see him when the city had not yet fallen.

sentences.zh: 繼隆度金陵破在旦夕，因言在途遇大風晦暝，城破之兆也。

translations.literal: Jilong judged Jinling's fall was imminent and said that on the road he had met great wind and dim sky—a sign the city would fall.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong judged Jinling would fall soon and said wind and dark sky on the road foretold it.

sentences.zh: 翌日，捷奏至，太祖召謂曰：「如汝所料矣。」

translations.literal: The next day the victory report arrived; Taizu summoned him and said: "As you foretold."
translations.idiomatic: The next day victory came; Taizu said, "As you foretold."

sentences.zh: 吳將盧絳聚眾萬餘，攻掠州縣，命繼隆招來之。

translations.literal: The Wu general Lu Jiang gathered more than ten thousand men and raided prefectures and counties; Jilong was ordered to summon him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wu general Lu Jiang gathered over ten thousand and raided; Jilong was ordered to summon his surrender.

sentences.zh: 江南平，錄功遷莊宅副使。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified his merit was recorded and he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Manor Estates.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan fell his merit was recorded and he became Vice Commissioner of the Manor Estates.

sentences.zh: 從幸西洛，改御營前後巡檢使。

translations.literal: On the imperial visit to the western capital he was changed to inspector before and after the Imperial Camp.
translations.idiomatic: On the western capital tour he became inspector of the Imperial Camp.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，改六宅使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was changed to Commissioner of the Six Residences.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 he became Commissioner of the Six Residences.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔與王文寶、李神祐、劉承珪同護浚京西河，又與梁迥、竇神寶治決河。

translations.literal: He was once ordered with Wang Wenbao, Li Shenyou, and Liu Chenggui jointly to supervise dredging of the western capital river, and again with Liang Jiong and Dou Shenbao to repair the burst Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Wang Wenbao and others to dredge the western capital river, and with Liang Jiong and Dou Shenbao to repair the Yellow River breach.

sentences.zh: 迥體肥碩，所乘舟弊不能濟，繼隆易以己舟。

translations.literal: Jiong was corpulent; the boat he rode was rotten and could not cross; Jilong gave him his own boat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was corpulent; his boat was rotten; Jilong gave him his own boat.

sentences.zh: 已而繼隆舟果覆，棲枯桑杪，賴他舟以度。

translations.literal: Soon after Jilong's boat indeed capsized; he clung to a dead mulberry top and relied on another boat to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong's boat soon capsized; he clung to a dead mulberry and was saved by another boat.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，為四面提舉都監，與李漢瓊領梯衝地道攻城西面，機石過其旁，從卒仆死，繼隆督戰無怠。

translations.literal: On the Taiyuan campaign he was overall supervisor of the four sides and with Li Hanqiong commanded scaling ladders and tunnel attacks on the west; catapult stones passed beside him and attendants fell dead, yet Jilong pressed the attack without slack.
translations.idiomatic: On the Taiyuan campaign he supervised the four sides; catapult stones killed attendants beside him, yet he pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 討幽州，與郭守文領先鋒，破契丹數千眾。

translations.literal: On the Youzhou campaign he with Guo Shouwen led the vanguard and broke several thousand Khitan troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the Youzhou campaign he and Guo Shouwen led the vanguard and routed thousands of Khitan.

sentences.zh: 及圍范陽，又與守文為先鋒，大敗其眾於湖翟河南。

translations.literal: When besieging Fanyang he again with Shouwen were vanguard and heavily defeated their forces south of the Hudi River.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Fanyang he and Shouwen again led the vanguard and routed the enemy south of the Hudi River.

sentences.zh: 後為鎮州都監，契丹犯邊，與崔翰諸將禦之。

translations.literal: Later he was overall supervisor of Zhenzhou; when the Khitan raided the border he with Cui Han and other generals resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Zhenzhou overall supervisor; when Khitan raided he resisted with Cui Han and others.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗授以陣圖，及臨陣有不便，眾以上命不可違。

translations.literal: At first Taizong gave him a battle array diagram; when they reached the field it was inconvenient; the troops said the imperial order could not be disobeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had given him a battle diagram; in the field it was unsuitable, but troops said the order could not be disobeyed.

sentences.zh: 繼隆曰：「事有應變，安可預定，設獲違詔之罪，請獨當也。」

translations.literal: Jilong said: "Affairs require adaptation—how can they be fixed in advance? If we incur the crime of disobeying the edict, let me alone bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Jilong said, "War requires adaptation—how fix it in advance? If disobedience is a crime, let me bear it alone."

sentences.zh: 即從宜而行，敗之於徐河。

translations.literal: He then acted as circumstances required and defeated them at the Xu River.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as circumstances required and won at the Xu River.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷宮苑使、領媯州刺史，護三交屯兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Commissioner of the Palace Park and acting prefect of Ji; he oversaw Sanjiao garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became Palace Park Commissioner and acting Ji prefect, overseeing Sanjiao garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 與潘美出征北邊，破靈丘縣，盡略其人以歸。

translations.literal: With Pan Mei he campaigned on the northern border, took Lingqiu county, and carried off all its people.
translations.idiomatic: With Pan Mei on the northern border he took Lingqiu and carried off its people.

sentences.zh: 改定州駐泊都監。

translations.literal: He was changed to overall supervisor stationed at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made overall supervisor at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗領兵出土鐙砦，與賊戰，獲牛羊、車帳甚眾。

translations.literal: He once led troops out of Tutie stockade, fought the enemy, and captured cattle, sheep, carts, and tents in great number.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops from Tutie stockade, fought, and captured much livestock and equipment.

sentences.zh: 詔書褒美。

translations.literal: An edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷叛，命繼隆與田仁朗、王侁率兵擊之。

translations.literal: When Li Jiyuan rebelled, Jilong was ordered with Tian Renlang and Wang You to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiyuan rebelled, Jilong was ordered with Tian Renlang and Wang You to attack.

sentences.zh: 四月，出銀州北，破悉利諸族，追奔數十里，斬三千餘級，俘蕃漢老幼千餘，梟代州刺史折羅遇及其弟埋乞首，牛馬、鎧仗所獲尤多。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he went north of Yinzhou, broke the Xili tribes, pursued several tens of li, beheaded more than three thousand, captured over a thousand Tangut and Han old and young, displayed the heads of the acting prefect of Dai, Zheluoyu, and his brother Maiqi, and booty of cattle, horses, and armor was especially great.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month north of Yinzhou he broke the Xili tribes, pursued tens of li, beheaded three thousand, took many captives, and displayed the heads of Zheluoyu and Maiqi with great booty.

sentences.zh: 又出開光穀西杏子坪，破保寺、保香族，斬其副首領埋乜已五十七人，降銀三族首領析八軍等三千餘眾，復破沒邵浪、悉訛諸族，及濁輪川東、兔頭川西，生擒七十八人，斬首五十九級，俘獲數千計。

translations.literal: He again went out west of Kaiguang valley to Apricot Flat, broke the Baosi and Baoxiang tribes, beheaded their deputy leaders including Maiyeyi—fifty-seven men—and the three Yin tribe leaders including Zhebajun and more than three thousand others submitted; he again broke the Moshaolang and Xiebo tribes and east of the Turbid Wheel River and west of Rabbit Head Mountain, taking seventy-eight alive and fifty-nine heads, with captives numbering in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He again struck west of Kaiguang valley, broke several tribes, took many heads and captives by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 引師至監城，吳移、越移四族來降，惟岌伽羅膩十四族怙其眾不下，乃與尹憲襲擊之，夷其帳千餘，俘斬七千餘級。

translations.literal: Leading the army to Jiancheng, the Wu Yi and Yue Yi four tribes came to submit; only the Yijiialuoni fourteen tribes, relying on their numbers, would not submit; he with Yin Xian attacked them and destroyed over a thousand tents, capturing and beheading more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiancheng four tribes submitted; fourteen tribes refused; he with Yin Xian destroyed over a thousand tents and beheaded seven thousand.

sentences.zh: 俄改領環州團練使，又護高陽關屯兵。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to regimental commander of Huanzhou and again oversaw Gaoyang Pass garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Huanzhou regimental commander and again oversaw Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 從曹彬征幽州，率兵助先鋒薛繼昭破其眾數千於固安南，下固安、新城，進克涿州，矢中左股，血流至踵，獲契丹貴臣一人。

translations.literal: On Cao Bin's Youzhou campaign he led troops to assist the vanguard Xue Jizhao in breaking several thousand of their forces south of Gu'an and took Gu'an and Xincheng, then captured Zhuozhou; an arrow struck his left thigh, blood flowed to his heel, and he captured a Khitan noble.
translations.idiomatic: On Cao Bin's Youzhou campaign he assisted Xue Jizhao, took Gu'an and Zhuozhou, was wounded in the thigh, and captured a Khitan noble.

sentences.zh: 彬欲上其功，繼隆止之。

translations.literal: Bin wished to report his merit; Jilong stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Bin wished to report his merit; Jilong refused.

sentences.zh: 俄而傅潛、米信軍敗眾潰，獨繼隆所部振旅而還。

translations.literal: Soon Fu Qian and Mi Xin's armies were defeated and the masses fled; only Jilong's command returned in good order.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fu Qian and Mi Xin were routed; only Jilong's command returned in order.

sentences.zh: 即命繼隆知定州，尋詔分屯諸軍，繼隆令書吏盡錄其詔。

translations.literal: He was immediately made prefect of Dingzhou; soon an edict divided the garrison troops and Jilong ordered clerks to record the entire edict.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Dingzhou prefect; when troops were divided he had clerks record the full edict.

sentences.zh: 旬餘，有敗卒集城下，不知所向，繼隆按詔給券，俾各持詣所部。

translations.literal: After ten-odd days defeated soldiers gathered below the wall not knowing where to go; Jilong checked the edict and gave each a voucher to go to his assigned command.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated soldiers gathered at the wall; Jilong issued vouchers per the edict to send each to his command.

sentences.zh: 太宗益嘉其有謀。

translations.literal: Taizong praised his resourcefulness the more.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised his resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷侍衛馬軍都虞候、領武州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Deputy Commander of the Palace Horse Army and Defender of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Deputy Commander of the Palace Horse Army and Defender of Wu.

sentences.zh: 契丹大入邊，出為滄州都部署。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided deeply, he was sent out as overall deployer of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan raided deeply he was overall deployer of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉廷讓與敵戰君子館，先約繼隆以精卒後殿，緩急為援。

translations.literal: Liu Tingrang fought the enemy at Junzi Pavilion; they had first agreed Jilong would follow with elite troops in the rear and aid in urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tingrang fought at Junzi Pavilion; Jilong had agreed to follow with elite rear guard.

sentences.zh: 既而敵圍廷讓數重，繼隆引麾下兵退保樂壽，廷讓力不敵，全軍陷沒，裁以單騎遁免。

translations.literal: The enemy surrounded Tingrang many layers deep; Jilong led his troops back to secure Le Shou; Tingrang could not match them and the whole army was lost; he barely escaped alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy surrounded Tingrang; Jilong withdrew to Le Shou; Tingrang's whole army was lost and he barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 上怒，追繼隆赴闕，令中書問狀，既而得釋。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and summoned Jilong to court to be questioned by the Secretariat; he was then released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and summoned Jilong for questioning; he was then released.

sentences.zh: 逾年，加領本州觀察使。

translations.literal: After a year he was given the additional post of military commissioner of his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was also made military commissioner of his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，製授侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領保順節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was made Commander of the Palace Horse Army and military commissioner of Baoshun.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Duangong he commanded the Palace Horse Army and held Baoshun.

sentences.zh: 九月，出為定州都部署。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was sent out as overall deployer of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was overall deployer of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，朝議有寇至，令堅壁清野，勿與戰。

translations.literal: At first court discussion held that if bandits came they should fortify and clear the countryside, not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Court policy was to fortify and clear the countryside, not fight.

sentences.zh: 一日，契丹驟至，攻滿城，至唐河。

translations.literal: One day the Khitan suddenly arrived, attacked Mancheng, and reached the Tang River.
translations.idiomatic: One day Khitan suddenly attacked Mancheng and reached the Tang River.

sentences.zh: 護軍袁繼忠慷慨請出師，中黃門林延壽等五人以詔書止之。

translations.literal: Protector Yuan Jizhong passionately requested to go out; the five eunuchs including Lin Yanshou used the edict to stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Protector Yuan Jizhong begged to fight; five eunuchs including Lin Yanshou stopped them by edict.

sentences.zh: 繼隆曰：「閫外之事，將帥得專。」

translations.literal: Jilong said: "Outside the gate, generals may decide for themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Jilong said, "Beyond the gate generals decide for themselves."

sentences.zh: 乃與繼忠出兵，戰數合，擊走之。

translations.literal: He then with Jizhong led troops out, fought several rounds, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jizhong led troops out, fought several rounds, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，送芻粟入威虜軍，蕃將於越率騎八萬來邀王師，繼隆所領步騎裁一萬，先命千人設伏城北十里，而與尹繼倫列陣以待。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year he escorted fodder into Weilu army; the barbarian general Yuyue led eighty thousand cavalry to intercept the Song army; Jilong's infantry and cavalry numbered only ten thousand; he first sent a thousand men to ambush ten li north of the city and with Yin Jilun arrayed to wait.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the second year he escorted fodder to Weilu; Yuyue led eighty thousand cavalry; Jilong had ten thousand and set an ambush ten li north with Yin Jilun.

sentences.zh: 敵眾方食，繼倫出其不意，擊走之。

translations.literal: The enemy were just eating when Jilun struck them unexpectedly and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: While the enemy ate, Jilun struck unexpectedly and routed them.

sentences.zh: 繼隆追奔過徐河，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Jilong pursued past the Xu River; captives were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong pursued past the Xu River with many captives.

sentences.zh: 嘗有詔廢威虜軍，繼隆言：「梁門為北面保障，不可廢。」

translations.literal: There had been an edict to abolish Weilu army; Jilong said: "Liang Gate is the north's bulwark—it cannot be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: An edict had abolished Weilu army; Jilong said Liang Gate was the north's bulwark and could not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 遂城守如故，訖為要地。

translations.literal: They therefore garrisoned and defended as before, and it remained a key point.
translations.idiomatic: They garrisoned as before and it remained a key post.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，上遣使至定州，密諭繼隆：「若契丹復入寇，朕當親討。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua the emperor sent an envoy to Dingzhou secretly telling Jilong: "If the Khitan raid again, I will campaign in person."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunhua the emperor secretly told Jilong he would campaign in person if Khitan raided again.

sentences.zh: 繼隆上奏曰：「自北邊肆孽，邊邑多虞，陛下不知臣不材，任以疆事，臣敢不講求軍實，震耀戎容，奉揚天聲，以遏外侮。

translations.literal: Jilong memorialized: "Since the northern border has suffered calamity, border towns are anxious; Your Majesty does not know my incompetence but entrusts me with frontier affairs—I dare not fail to seek military strength, display martial might, uphold Heaven's prestige, and check foreign insult.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong memorialized that he would uphold Heaven's prestige and check the barbarians without troubling the emperor to campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 然臣奉辭之日，曾瀝愚衷，誠以蜂蟻之妖，必就鯨鯢之戮。

translations.literal: Yet when I received my commission I once poured out my sincere heart, truly believing such hornet and ant troubles would surely meet whale destruction.
translations.idiomatic: He had pledged that small foes would meet destruction.

sentences.zh: 臣子之分，死生以之，望不議於親巡，庶靡勞於天步，今聆聖誨，將決親征，且一人既行，百司景從，次舍驅馳，郡縣供饋，勞費滋甚。

translations.literal: A subject's portion is to stake life and death on it; I hope you will not discuss a personal tour, lest the imperial steps be troubled.
translations.idiomatic: He begged the emperor not to tour in person lest the court be burdened.

sentences.zh: 殄此微妖，當責將帥，臣雖駑弱，誓死為期。」

translations.literal: Now I hear the sage instruction and a personal campaign is decided; with one man going, a hundred offices follow in train, lodging and supply press on the prefectures and counties—expense grows greatly.
translations.idiomatic: A personal campaign would burden the realm; he would die to destroy the foe instead.

sentences.zh: 是歲，契丹不入邊，議遂止。

translations.literal: To destroy this petty evil should be charged to the generals; though I am weak, I vow to die on schedule."
translations.idiomatic: He vowed to die on schedule if the generals were trusted.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，召還，太宗面獎之，改領靜難軍節度，復遣還屯所。

translations.literal: That year the Khitan did not enter the border and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: That year Khitan did not raid and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時夏州趙保忠與繼遷連謀，朝廷患之，又綏州牙校高文岯舉城效順，河外蕃漢大擾，以繼隆為河西行營都部署、尚食使尹繼隆為都監以討之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year he was recalled; Taizong praised him to his face and changed him to military commissioner of the Jingnan army, then sent him back to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer he was recalled, praised, made Jingnan military commissioner, and sent back.

sentences.zh: 既而繼遷遁去，擒保忠以獻。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Baozhong of Xiazhou and Jiyuan were in league; the court was troubled; also Suizhou officer Gao Wenpi offered the city in submission; the outer tribes were greatly disturbed; Jilong was made overall deployer of the Hexi field army and Yin Jilong overall supervisor to attack.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiazhou in turmoil and Gao Wenpi submitting, Jilong was made Hexi overall deployer with Yin Jilong as supervisor.

sentences.zh: 初，裨將侯延廣、監軍秦翰議請誅保忠，及出兵追之，繼隆曰：「保忠杌上肉爾，當請於天子。

translations.literal: Soon Jiyuan fled; Baozhong was captured and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiyuan fled and Baozhong was captured.

sentences.zh: 今繼遷遁去，千里窮磧，艱於轉餉，宜養威持重，未易輕舉。」

translations.literal: At first the lieutenant Hou Yanguang and inspector Qin Han discussed requesting Baozhong be executed; when troops went out to pursue, Jilong said: "Baozhong is meat on the chopping block—we should request the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Officers wished to kill Baozhong; Jilong said he was meat on the block and they should ask the emperor.

sentences.zh: 延廣等服其言。

translations.literal: Now Jiyuan has fled; a thousand li of barren desert makes supply hard—we should build power and hold steady, not act lightly."
translations.idiomatic: With Jiyuan fled and supply hard across desert, they should hold steady.

sentences.zh: 會密詔廢夏州，隳其城。

translations.literal: Yanguang and the others accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 繼隆命秦翰與弟繼和及高繼勳同入奏，以為朔方古鎮，賊所窺覦之地，存之可依以破賊；

translations.literal: A secret edict arrived to abolish Xiazhou and destroy its walls.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict came to abolish Xiazhou and destroy its walls.

sentences.zh: 並請於銀、夏兩州南界山中增置保戍，以扼其衝，且為內屬蕃部之障蔽，而斷賊糧運。

translations.literal: Jilong ordered Qin Han with his brother Jihe and Gao Jixun to enter court together, holding that Shuofang was an ancient post the enemy coveted—keeping it could break the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Jilong sent Qin Han, Jihe, and Gao Jixun to court arguing Xiazhou should be kept to break the enemy.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: they also requested adding garrison posts in the mountains south of Yin and Xia to choke their route and shield inner tribes while cutting enemy grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: They asked for garrison posts south of Yin and Xia to choke routes and cut supplies.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，白守宗守榮、馬紹忠等送糧靈州，為繼遷所邀，敗於洛浦河。

translations.literal: None was answered.
translations.idiomatic: None was granted.

sentences.zh: 上聞之怒，亟命繼隆為靈、環十州都部署。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, Bai Shouzong, Ma Shaozhong, and others escorted grain to Lingzhou and were intercepted by Jiyuan and defeated at the Luopu River.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 2 grain escorts were intercepted by Jiyuan and defeated at Luopu River.

sentences.zh: 是秋，五路討繼遷，以繼隆出環州，取東關鎮，由赤檉、苦井路赴之。

translations.literal: On hearing this the emperor was angry and urgently ordered Jilong overall deployer of the ten Ling and Huan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in anger made Jilong overall deployer of ten Ling and Huan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 繼隆以所出道回遠乏水，請由橐駝路徑趨賊之巢穴。

translations.literal: That autumn the five-route campaign against Jiyuan had Jilong exit Huanzhou, take Dongguan post, and go by Red Tallow and Bitter Well roads.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn's five-route campaign had Jilong exit Huanzhou by Red Tallow and Bitter Well roads.

sentences.zh: 且遣繼和入奏，太宗召詰之，知其必敗，因遣周瑩齎手詔切責，督其進軍赤檉。

translations.literal: Jilong held the route too long and waterless and requested the camel route straight at the enemy nest.
translations.idiomatic: The route was long and waterless; he requested the camel route straight at the enemy.

sentences.zh: 瑩至，繼隆以便宜發兵，不俟報，與丁罕行十餘日，果不見賊而還。

translations.literal: He also sent Jihe to report; Taizong summoned and questioned him, knew they would surely fail, and sent Zhou Ying with a hand edict sternly reproving and urging advance on Red Tallow.
translations.idiomatic: Jihe reported; Taizong knew they would fail and sent Zhou Ying with a stern edict to advance on Red Tallow.

sentences.zh: 諸將失期，士卒困乏。

translations.literal: When Ying arrived Jilong mobilized on his own authority without awaiting reply and with Ding Han marched ten-odd days and indeed saw no enemy and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ying arrived; Jilong marched without awaiting reply, saw no enemy in ten days, and returned.

sentences.zh: 繼隆素剛，因慚憤，肆殺戮，乃奏轉運使陳絳、梁鼎軍儲不繼，並坐削秩。

translations.literal: The generals missed the deadline and troops were weary.
translations.idiomatic: Generals missed deadlines; troops were weary.

sentences.zh: 三年春，繼遷以蕃部從順者眾，遣其軍主史乚遇率兵屯橐駝口西北雙雉，以遏絕之。

translations.literal: Jilong was by nature stubborn; from shame and anger he wantonly killed and memorialized that transport commissioners Chen Jiang and Liang Ding failed to supply the army; both were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and angry, Jilong wantonly killed and blamed transport commissioners Chen Jiang and Liang Ding, who were demoted.

sentences.zh: 執倉族蕃官乚遇來告，繼隆遣劉承蘊、田敏會乚遇討之，斬首數千級，獲牛馬、橐駝萬計。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year Jiyuan, because many tribes had submitted, sent his commander Shiyiyu to hold Shuangzhi northwest of Camel Mouth to block them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the third year Jiyuan sent Shiyiyu to block submitting tribes at Shuangzhi.

sentences.zh: 先是，受詔送軍糧赴靈州，必由旱海路，自冬至春，而芻粟始集。

translations.literal: The Zhi tribal officer Yiyu came to report; Jilong sent Liu Chengyun and Tian Min with Yiyu to attack; they beheaded several thousand and took cattle, horses, and camels by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyu reported; Jilong sent Liu Chengyun and Tian Min to attack and took vast booty.

sentences.zh: 繼隆請由古原州蔚茹河路便，眾議不一，繼隆固執論其事，太宗許焉。

translations.literal: Earlier he had received orders to escort army grain to Lingzhou, which had to go by the Dry Sea road from winter to spring before fodder was gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Grain to Lingzhou had to go by the Dry Sea road from winter to spring.

sentences.zh: 遂率師以進，壁古原州，令如京使胡守澄城之，是為鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: Jilong requested the ancient Yuanzhou Weiru River route as convenient; opinion was divided but Jilong firmly argued and Taizong assented.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong requested the Weiru River route; Taizong assented.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，改領鎮安軍節度、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded he was changed to military commissioner of the Zhen'an army and Honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded he became Zhen'an military commissioner and Honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 逾月召還，加同中書門下平章事，解兵柄歸本鎮。

translations.literal: Within a month he was recalled and given Tong zhongshu menxia pingzhangshi and released from military power to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was recalled, made Chief Councilor, and released from military command.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，丁內艱，起復。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he mourned his mother and was recalled to service.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2 he mourned his mother and was recalled to service.

sentences.zh: 會秋潦暴集，蔡水壞岸，繼隆乘危督士卒補塞，自辰訖午，衝波稍息。

translations.literal: When autumn floods burst the Cai River banks Jilong braved danger supervising soldiers to plug the breach; from morning to noon the rushing waves gradually eased.
translations.idiomatic: When floods burst the Cai River he braved danger plugging the breach until noon.

sentences.zh: 四年，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was given Honorary Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was given Honorary Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 王師失利於望都，繼隆累表求詣闕面陳邊事，因乞自效。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated at Wangdu Jilong repeatedly memorialized requesting audience to state border affairs and begged to serve in person.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat at Wangdu he repeatedly begged audience and to serve in person.

sentences.zh: 俄召還，延見詢訪，因言：「醜類侵擾，蓋亦常事，願委將帥討伐，不煩親征。」

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled; on audience and inquiry he said: "The ugly sort raid—this too is ordinary; please entrust generals to campaign—no need for a personal expedition."
translations.idiomatic: Soon recalled at audience he said barbarian raids were ordinary and urged entrusting generals rather than personal expedition.

sentences.zh: 真宗慰諭之，改山南東道節度，判許州。

translations.literal: Zhenzong comforted him and changed him to military commissioner of the Shannan East circuit and acting prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong comforted him and made him Shannan East military commissioner at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，明德皇太后不豫，詔入省疾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, Empress Dowager Mingde was ill and an edict ordered him to visit her sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde Empress Dowager Mingde was ill and he was ordered to visit.

sentences.zh: 九月，復許會葬。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was again permitted to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was permitted to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 是冬，契丹大入，逾魏郡至河上。

translations.literal: That winter the Khitan raided deeply, passed Wei command to the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Khitan raided deeply past Wei to the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 真宗幸澶淵，繼隆表求扈從，命為駕前東西排陣使，先赴澶州，陳師於北城外，毀車為營。

translations.literal: Zhenzong went to Chanyuan; Jilong memorialized asking to escort and was made Front East-West Array Commander before the imperial carriage, first sent to Chanyuan to array troops north of the outer city and destroy carts to make camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong went to Chanyuan; Jilong asked to escort, was made Front Array Commander, went first to Chanyuan, arrayed troops north of the city, and made camp from carts.

sentences.zh: 敵數萬騎急攻，繼隆與石保吉率眾禦之，追奔數里。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of enemy cavalry attacked fiercely; Jilong with Shi Baoji led troops to resist and pursued several li.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of enemy cavalry attacked; Jilong and Shi Baoji resisted and pursued several li.

sentences.zh: 及上至，幸北門觀兵，召問慰勞，見其所部整肅，歎賞久之。

translations.literal: When the emperor arrived he visited the north gate to review troops, summoned and comforted him, saw his command orderly, and sighed in praise for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived he reviewed troops at the north gate, summoned and comforted Jilong, saw his command orderly, and praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 翌日，幸營中，召從臣飲宴。

translations.literal: The next day he visited the camp and summoned attendant ministers to drink.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he visited the camp and feasted his ministers.

sentences.zh: 二年春，還京，加開府儀同三司、食邑、實封。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he returned to the capital and was given Grandee of the Palace with fief salary and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second spring he returned to the capital and was given Grandee of the Palace with fief salary and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 詔始下，會疾作，上親臨問。

translations.literal: The edict had just issued when illness struck; the emperor personally visited to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The edict had just been issued when he fell ill; the emperor visited him in person.

sentences.zh: 繼和時為幷、代鈐轄，驛召省視。

translations.literal: Jihe was then military controller of Bing and Dai; he was summoned by post to visit.
translations.idiomatic: Jihe was then military controller of Bing and Dai and was summoned by express post to visit.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨哭之慟，為制服發哀。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage came in person to mourn him bitterly, wore mourning garments, and expressed grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn him bitterly, wore mourning, and grieved.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令，諡忠武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Palace Secretariat and given the posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Palace Secretariat with the posthumous title Loyal Martial.

sentences.zh: 以其子昭慶為洛苑使，從子昭嗣、昭遜，並為內殿崇班。

translations.literal: His son Zhaoqing was made Commissioner of the Luoyuan; his collateral nephews Zhaosi and Zhaoxun were both made Inner Hall Honored Class.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaoqing became Luoyuan Commissioner; his nephews Zhaosi and Zhaoxun became Inner Hall Honored Class.

sentences.zh: 又錄其門下二十餘人。

translations.literal: More than twenty men of his household were also recorded.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty household members were also given office.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，詔與李沆，王旦同配享真宗廟庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing an edict ordered him honored with Li Fang and Wang Dan in the temple of Zhenzong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianxing he was ordered honored with Li Fang and Wang Dan in Zhenzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 繼隆出貴胄，善騎射，曉音律，感慨自樹，深沉有城府，嚴於御下。

translations.literal: Jilong came from a noble house, was skilled at riding and shooting, understood music, was stirred to establish himself, was deep and had schemes, and was strict in commanding subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong was of noble birth, skilled at riding, shooting, and music, ambitious and deep-scheming, strict with subordinates.

sentences.zh: 好讀《春秋左氏傳》，喜名譽，賓禮儒士。

translations.literal: He loved reading the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, delighted in reputation, and treated scholar-officials with guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He read the Zuo Commentary, sought reputation, and honored scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 在太宗朝，特被親信，每征行，必委以機要。

translations.literal: In Taizong's reign he was especially trusted; on every campaign he was entrusted with crucial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong he was especially trusted with crucial affairs on every campaign.

sentences.zh: 真宗以元舅之親，不欲煩以軍旅，優遊近藩，恩禮甚篤。

translations.literal: Zhenzong, as maternal uncle, did not wish to burden him with armies and let him enjoy ease in a nearby command with deep favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong, as maternal uncle, kept him at ease in a nearby command with deep favor.

sentences.zh: 然多智用，能謙謹保身。

translations.literal: Yet he was resourceful and knew how to be modest and preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was resourceful and knew how to preserve himself.

sentences.zh: 明德寢疾，欲面見之，上促其往。

translations.literal: When Mingde lay ill she wished to see him face to face; the emperor urged him to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingde lay ill she wished to see him; the emperor urged him to go.

sentences.zh: 繼隆但詣萬安宮門拜箋，終不入。

translations.literal: Jilong only went to the Wan'an Palace gate to present a written greeting and never entered.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong only bowed with a written greeting at Wan'an Palace gate and never entered.

sentences.zh: 又嘗命諸王詣第候謁，繼隆不設湯茗，第假王府從行茶爐烹飲焉。

translations.literal: He was also once ordered to have the princes call at his residence; Jilong set out no tea but borrowed the princes' traveling tea stove to brew.
translations.idiomatic: When princes were ordered to call on him, he set out no tea but borrowed their traveling stove.

sentences.zh: 昭慶改名昭亮，至東上閤門使、高州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhaoqing changed his name to Zhaoliang and reached Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate and prefect of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoqing renamed Zhaoliang and became Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Gao.

sentences.zh: 子 繼和

translations.literal: Son Jihe
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jihe

sentences.zh: 繼和，字周叔，少以蔭補供奉官，三遷洛苑使。

translations.literal: Jihe, styled Zhoushu, in youth entered office by privilege as Honored Attendant and was transferred three times to Commissioner of the Luoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jihe, styled Zhoushu, entered by privilege as Honored Attendant and rose to Luoyuan Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 淳化後，繼隆多在邊任，繼和常從行，友愛尤至，每令入奏機事。

translations.literal: After Chunhua, Jilong was often on the border and Jihe often followed, loving each other especially; he was often ordered to enter court and report military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Chunhua Jilong was often on the border; Jihe followed, loved him dearly, and often reported military affairs at court.

sentences.zh: 繼隆罷兵柄，手錄唐李勣遺戒授繼和，曰：「吾門不墜者在爾矣。」

translations.literal: When Jilong relinquished military power he hand-copied Li Ji's deathbed admonition and gave it to Jihe, saying: "Our house not falling rests on you."
translations.idiomatic: When Jilong gave up military power he copied Li Ji's deathbed admonition for Jihe: "Our house rests on you."

sentences.zh: 初，繼隆之請城鎮戎軍也，朝廷不果於行。

translations.literal: At first when Jilong requested to wall Zhenrong army the court did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: When Jilong first asked to wall Zhenrong army the court did not act.

sentences.zh: 繼和面奏曰：「平涼舊地，山川阻險，旁扼夷落，為中華襟帶，城之為便。」

translations.literal: Jihe memorialized in person: "The old Pingliang territory has dangerous mountains and rivers, flanks the barbarian settlements, and is the girdle of China—walling it is advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: Jihe memorialized: old Pingliang was strategically vital—walling it was wise.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃許焉。

translations.literal: Taizong then assented.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then agreed.

sentences.zh: 後復不守。

translations.literal: Later it was again not held.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was abandoned again.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，繼和又以為言，乃命版築，以繼和知其軍，兼原、渭、儀都巡檢使。

translations.literal: In Xianping Jihe again spoke and they ordered construction; Jihe was made to know its army and concurrently overall inspector of Yuan, Wei, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping Jihe spoke again; they built it and made him commander with inspection of Yuan, Wei, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 城畢，加領平州刺史。

translations.literal: When the wall was complete he was given the additional post of prefect of Ping.
translations.idiomatic: When the wall was done he was also made prefect of Ping.

sentences.zh: 建議募貧民及弓箭手，墾田積粟，又屢請益兵，朝議未許。

translations.literal: He proposed recruiting poor people and archers to open fields and store grain and repeatedly requested more troops; court discussion did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed recruiting poor men and archers to farm and store grain and asked for more troops; court refused.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「苟緩急，部署不為濟師，則或至失援矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If there is urgency and the deployer does not reinforce, one may even lose support."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said if urgency came and the deployer failed to reinforce, support could be lost.

sentences.zh: 命繼和兼涇、原、儀、渭鈐轄。

translations.literal: He ordered Jihe to concurrently control Jing, Yuan, Yi, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jihe to control Jing, Yuan, Yi, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 時繼遷未弭，命張齊賢、梁顥經略，因訪繼和邊事。

translations.literal: At the time Jiyuan was not yet pacified; Zhang Qixian and Liang Hao were ordered to manage affairs and consulted Jihe on border matters.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiyuan unrest, Zhang Qixian and Liang Hao consulted Jihe on border affairs.

sentences.zh: 繼和上言：

translations.literal: Jihe memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Jihe memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「鎮戎軍為涇、原、儀、渭北面扞蔽，又為環、慶、原、渭、儀、秦熟戶所依，正當回鶻、西涼、六穀、吐蕃、咩逋、賤遇、馬臧、梁家諸族之路。

translations.literal: "Zhenrong army is the northern shield of Jing, Yuan, Yi, and Wei and what the settled households of Huan, Qing, Yuan, Wei, Yi, and Qin rely on; it lies on the routes of the Uighurs, Western Liang, the Six Valleys, Tibet, Mipo, Jingyou, Mazang, the Liang clan, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhenrong army shields Jing, Yuan, Yi, and Wei and shelters settled tribes on routes of Uighurs, Tibet, and many others.

sentences.zh: 自置軍已來，克張邊備，方於至道中所葺，今已數倍。

translations.literal: Since the army was established the border defense has expanded; compared with what was built in the Zhidao era it is now several times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Since it was built defenses have multiplied several times over the Zhidao era.

sentences.zh: 誠能常用步騎五千守之，涇、原、渭州苟有緩急，會於此軍，並力戰守，則賊必不敢過此軍；

translations.literal: If five thousand infantry and cavalry are permanently stationed, when Jing, Yuan, and Wei are in trouble they can assemble here and fight together, and the enemy will not dare pass this army;
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand troops stationed here could unite the circuit in crisis and block the enemy.

sentences.zh: 而緣邊民戶不廢耕織，熟戶老幼有所歸宿。

translations.literal: then border households will not cease farming and settled households old and young will have refuge.
