translations.idiomatic: Border farmers could keep farming and families would have refuge.

sentences.zh: 此軍苟廢，則過此新城，止皆廢壘。

translations.literal: If this army is abolished, beyond this new city all will be abandoned ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: "If it is abolished, beyond the new city lie only abandoned walls."

sentences.zh: 有數路來寇：若自隴山下南去，則由三百堡入儀州製勝關；

translations.literal: Several routes of enemy attack: from south of Longshan, through Three Hundred Forts into Yizhou's Zhicheng Pass;
translations.idiomatic: "Enemy routes include from Longshan through Three Hundred Forts to Yizhou;"

sentences.zh: 自瓦亭路南去，則由彈箏峽入渭州安國鎮；

translations.literal: from south of Wating, through Tanqi Gorge into Weizhou's Anguo post;
translations.idiomatic: "from Wating through Tanqi Gorge to Weizhou;"

sentences.zh: 自清石嶺東南去，則由小盧、大盧、潘穀入潘原縣；

translations.literal: from southeast of Qingshi Ridge, through Little Lu, Great Lu, and Pan valleys into Panyuan county;
translations.idiomatic: "from Qingshi Ridge through Lu and Pan valleys to Panyuan;"

sentences.zh: 若至潘原而西則入渭州，東則入涇州；

translations.literal: if they reach Panyuan and go west they enter Weizhou, east they enter Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: "from Panyuan west to Wei, east to Jing;"

sentences.zh: 若自東石嶺東公主泉南去，則由東山砦故彭陽城西並入原州；

translations.literal: if from east of East Stone Ridge and south of Princess Spring, through East Mountain stockade and old Pengyang city west into Yuanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: "from East Stone Ridge and Princess Spring through East Mountain to Yuanzhou;"

sentences.zh: 其餘細路不可盡數。

translations.literal: the other small routes cannot all be numbered.
translations.idiomatic: "countless lesser routes besides."

sentences.zh: 如以五千步騎，令四州各為備禦，不相會合，則兵勢分而力不足禦矣。

translations.literal: If five thousand infantry and cavalry are divided so each of the four prefectures defends separately without joining, military power is scattered and strength insufficient to resist.
translations.idiomatic: "Dividing five thousand among four prefectures would scatter strength."

sentences.zh: 故置此城以扼要路。

translations.literal: Therefore this city is placed to choke the crucial routes.
translations.idiomatic: "Hence this city chokes the crucial routes."

sentences.zh: 即令自靈、環、慶、鄜、延、石、隰、麟、府等州以外河曲之地，皆屬於賊，若更攻陷靈州，西取回鶻，則吐蕃震懼，皆為吞噬，西北邊民，將受驅劫。

translations.literal: Even if beyond Ling, Huan, Qing, Fu, Yan, Shi, Zhi, Lin, and Fu and the bend of the river all belonged to the enemy, if Lingzhou too fell and they took the Uighurs west, Tibet would tremble and all be swallowed—northwest border people would be driven and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: "Even if the whole northwest fell, losing Lingzhou would let the enemy swallow Tibet and drive the border people."

sentences.zh: 若以可惜之地，甘受賊攻，便思委棄，以為良策，是則有盡之地，不能供無已之求也。

translations.literal: If for land one grudges losing to enemy attack one thinks abandonment a good plan, then finite land cannot supply endless demands.
translations.idiomatic: "To abandon land because the enemy attacks finite ground cannot satisfy endless loss."

sentences.zh: 臣慮議者以調發芻糧擾民為言，則此軍所費，上出四川，地里非遙，輸送甚易。

translations.literal: I fear those who cite fodder transport troubling the people; this army's cost comes from Sichuan, the distance is not far, and transport is easy.
translations.idiomatic: "Fodder cost is borne by Sichuan and transport is easy."

sentences.zh: 又劉琮方興屯田，屯田若成，積中有備，則四州稅物，亦不須得。

translations.literal: Also Liu Cong is opening military colonies; if colonies succeed and stores fill, the four prefectures' tax goods may not be needed.
translations.idiomatic: "Liu Cong's colonies may make the four prefectures' taxes unnecessary."

sentences.zh: 況今繼遷強盛，有逾曩日。

translations.literal: Moreover Jiyuan is now stronger than in former days.
translations.idiomatic: "Jiyuan is stronger than before."

sentences.zh: 從靈州至原、渭、儀州界，次更取棨子山以西接環州山內及平夏，次並黃河以東以南、隴山內外接儀州界，及靈州以北河外。

translations.literal: From Lingzhou to the borders of Yuan, Wei, and Yi, then west of Zizi Mountain connecting Huanzhou's inner ranges and Pingxia, then east and south of the Yellow River and inside Longshan connecting Yizhou, and north of Lingzhou beyond the river—
translations.idiomatic: "From Lingzhou through Yuan, Wei, Yi, Zizi Mountain, the Yellow River bend, and beyond—"

sentences.zh: 蕃部約數十萬帳，賊來足以鬥敵，賊遷未盛，不敢深入。

translations.literal: tribal households number in the hundreds of thousands; when enemies come they suffice to fight; when Jiyuan was not strong they dared not penetrate deeply.
translations.idiomatic: "tribes numbered in the hundreds of thousands and once sufficed to fight; when Jiyuan was weak they dared not penetrate."

sentences.zh: 今則靈州北河外，鎮戎軍、環州並北徹靈武、平夏及山外黃河以東族帳，悉為繼遷所吞，縱有一二十族，殘破奔迸，事力十無二三。

translations.literal: Now north of Lingzhou beyond the river, Zhenrong army, Huanzhou, and north through Lingwu, Pingxia, and tribes east of the Yellow River have nearly all been swallowed by Jiyuan; even one or two clans remain broken and fleeing, their strength one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: "Now most tribes beyond Lingzhou have been swallowed; survivors are one in ten."

sentences.zh: 自官軍瀚海失利，賊愈猖狂，群蕃震懼，絕無鬥志。

translations.literal: Since the Hanhai defeat the enemy grows more arrogant and tribes are terrified without fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: "Since Hanhai defeat the enemy grows bold and tribes have lost spirit."

sentences.zh: 兼以咸平二年棄鎮戎後，繼遷徑來侵掠軍界蕃族，南至渭州安國鎮北一二十里，西至南市界三百餘里，便於蕭關屯聚萬子、米逋、西鼠等三千，以脅原、渭、靈、環熟戶，常時族帳謀歸賊者甚多。

translations.literal: Moreover since abandoning Zhenrong in Xianping 2 Jiyuan came straight to plunder tribal territory south to within ten or twenty li of Weizhou's Anguo post and west three hundred-odd li to Nanshi—he stationed Wanzi, Mipo, and Xishu at Xiaoguan, thirty thousand strong, to coerce Yuan, Wei, Ling, and Huan settled households; many clans often plotted to join the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: "Since Zhenrong was abandoned in Xianping 2 Jiyuan raided to Weizhou and stationed thirty thousand at Xiaoguan to coerce tribes."

sentences.zh: 賴聖謨深遠，不惑群議，復置此軍，一年以來，蕃部咸以安集，邊民無復愁苦。

translations.literal: Thanks to the sage's far sight, not confused by collective opinion, restoring this army, in one year tribes have all settled and border people no longer suffer.
translations.idiomatic: "Thanks to restoring this army, in one year tribes settled and border people were relieved."

sentences.zh: 以此較之，則存廢之說，相失萬倍矣。

translations.literal: Comparing these, the arguments for keeping or abolishing differ ten thousandfold.
translations.idiomatic: "Keeping or abolishing differs ten thousandfold."

sentences.zh: 又靈州遠絕，居常非有尺布鬥粟以供王府，今關西老幼，疲苦轉餉，所以不可棄者，誠恐滋大賊勢，使繼遷西取秦、成之群蕃，北掠回鶻之健馬，長驅南牧，何以枝梧。

translations.literal: Also Lingzhou is remote and normally has not a foot of cloth or peck of grain for the court; now the aged of Guanxi weary at transport—what cannot be abandoned is truly fear the enemy will grow and Jiyuan will take Qin and Cheng tribes west and seize Uighur horses north and drive south long—how to resist.
translations.idiomatic: "Lingzhou is remote yet cannot be abandoned lest Jiyuan seize tribes and horses and drive south unchecked."

sentences.zh: 昨朝廷訪問臣送芻糧道路，臣欲自蕭關至鎮戎城砦，西就胡盧河川運送。

translations.literal: When the court asked about my fodder route I wished to go from Xiaoguan to Zhenrong stockades and west along the Hulu River.
translations.idiomatic: "I wished to transport from Xiaoguan along the Hulu River."

sentences.zh: 但恐靈州食盡，或至不守，清遠固亦難保，青岡、白馬曷足禦扞，則環州便為極邊。

translations.literal: But I fear if Lingzhou's grain is exhausted it may not be held, Qingyuan too will be hard to keep, Qinggang and Baima cannot defend, and Huanzhou becomes the extreme border.
translations.idiomatic: "If Lingzhou's grain fails, Qingyuan and the passes fall and Huanzhou becomes the frontier."

sentences.zh: 若賊從蕭關、武延、石門路入鎮戎，縱有五七千兵，亦恐不敵，即回鶻、西涼路亦斷絕。

translations.literal: If the enemy enters by Xiaoguan, Wuyan, and Shimen routes into Zhenrong, even five or seven thousand troops may not suffice, and Uighur and Western Liang routes will also be cut.
translations.idiomatic: "If the enemy enters by Xiaoguan and Shimen, even thousands may not hold and western routes will be cut."

sentences.zh: 伏見咸平三年詔書，緣邊不得出兵生事蕃夷，蓋謂賊如猛獸，不怫其心，必且不動。

translations.literal: I have seen the Xianping 3 edict that the border must not send troops to provoke tribes, meaning the enemy is like a fierce beast—do not anger its heart and it may not move.
translations.idiomatic: "The Xianping 3 edict forbade provoking tribes lest the enemy, like a beast, be stirred."

sentences.zh: 臣愚慮此賊他日愈熾，不若聽驍將銳旅屢入其境，彼或聚兵自固，則勿與鬥，妖黨才散，則令掩擊。

translations.literal: I foolishly consider that if this enemy grows stronger later, it were better to let fierce generals and sharp armies enter their territory repeatedly; if they mass to hold firm, do not fight; when their rabble scatters, strike.
translations.idiomatic: "Better to raid repeatedly, fight only when they scatter."

sentences.zh: 如此則王師逸而賊兵勞，賊心內離，然後大舉。

translations.literal: Thus imperial troops rest while enemy troops labor and enemy hearts divide within—then strike in force.
translations.idiomatic: "Thus our troops rest, theirs labor, then strike in force."

sentences.zh: 及靈州孤壘，戍守最苦，望比他州尤加存恤。

translations.literal: Moreover Lingzhou's lonely rampart has the hardest garrison—I hope it receive more care than other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: "Lingzhou's garrison is hardest—I beg extra care."

sentences.zh: 且守邊之臣，內憂家屬之窘匱，外憂奸邪之憎毀。

translations.literal: Border officers inwardly worry their families' want and outwardly worry slander by the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: "Border officers fear family want and slander."

sentences.zh: 憂家則思為不廉，憂身則思為退跡，思不廉則官局不治，思退跡則庶事無心，欲其奮不顧身，令出惟行，不可得已。

translations.literal: Worrying for family they think of dishonesty; worrying for self they think of retreat; thinking dishonesty the office is not governed; thinking retreat nothing is undertaken with heart—wishing them to fight heedless of body and orders executed without fail cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: "Family worry breeds corruption; self worry breeds retreat—heedless courage cannot be expected."

sentences.zh: 良由賞未厚、恩未深也。

translations.literal: Truly rewards are not thick and grace not deep.
translations.idiomatic: "Rewards are not thick nor grace deep."

sentences.zh: 賞厚則人無顧內之憂，恩深則士有效死之志。

translations.literal: Thick rewards then men have no inward worry; deep grace then soldiers have will to die.
translations.idiomatic: "Thick rewards end inward worry; deep grace wins men who will die."

sentences.zh: 古之帝王皆懸爵賞以拔英俊，卒能成大功。

translations.literal: Ancient emperors all hung rank and reward to raise the outstanding and finally achieved great merit.
translations.idiomatic: "Ancient emperors hung rank and reward to achieve great merit."

sentences.zh: 大凡君子求名，小人徇利。

translations.literal: Generally gentlemen seek fame, small men pursue profit.
translations.idiomatic: "Gentlemen seek fame, small men profit."

sentences.zh: 臣為兒童時，嘗聞齊州防禦使李漢超守關南，齊州屬州城錢七八萬貫，悉以給與，非次賞賚，動及千萬。

translations.literal: When I was a child I once heard Li Hanchao, Defender of Guannan in Qizhou, held Qizhou's city money of seventy or eighty million strings and gave it all out, with extraordinary rewards often reaching ten million.
translations.idiomatic: "As a child I heard Li Hanchao gave Qizhou's seventy or eighty million strings in pay and huge rewards."

sentences.zh: 漢超猶私販榷場，規免商算，當時有以此事達於太祖者，即詔漢超私物所在，悉免關征。

translations.literal: Hanchao still privately traded at the border market to evade commercial tax; when this reached Taizu he issued an edict that wherever Hanchao's private goods went, all border tax was waived.
translations.idiomatic: "Hanchao even evaded border tax; Taizu waived tax on his private goods."

sentences.zh: 故漢超居則營生，戰則誓死，貲產厚則心有所係，必死戰則動有成績。

translations.literal: Therefore Hanchao at peace managed livelihood and in battle vowed death; thick assets then the heart has ties; sure death in battle then deeds succeed.
translations.idiomatic: "Hanchao farmed in peace and fought to the death; wealth bound his heart to victory."

sentences.zh: 故畢太祖之世，一方為之安靜。

translations.literal: Thus through Taizu's age one region was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: "Thus Taizu's age knew one region's peace."

sentences.zh: 今如漢超之材固亦不少，苟能用皇祖之遺法，選擇英傑，使守靈武，高官厚賞，不吝先與；

translations.literal: Today men like Hanchao are not few; if the imperial grandfather's legacy method is used to choose heroes to hold Lingzhou, high office and thick reward given generously in advance;
translations.idiomatic: "Men like Hanchao exist; use the founding method, choose heroes for Lingzhou, reward generously in advance;"

sentences.zh: 往日，留半奉給其家，半奉資其用，然後可以責潔廉之節，保必勝之功也。

translations.literal: in former days leave half salary for their families, half salary for their use, then one can demand clean integrity and assured victory.
translations.idiomatic: "leave half pay for family, half for use, then demand integrity and victory."

sentences.zh: 又戎事內製，或失權宜，漢時渤海盜起，龔遂為太守，尚聽便宜從事。

translations.literal: Also when military affairs are controlled from within one may miss what is fitting; when bandits rose in Bohai in Han times, Gong Sui as prefect was still allowed discretionary action.
translations.idiomatic: "Central control misses fit; even Gong Sui had discretion against Bohai bandits."

sentences.zh: 且渤海，漢之內地，盜賊，國之饑民；

translations.literal: Moreover Bohai was Han inner territory and bandits starving people of the state;
translations.idiomatic: "Bohai was inner Han territory and bandits were starving people;"

sentences.zh: 況靈武絕塞，西鄙強戎，又非渤海之比。

translations.literal: how much more is Lingwu a remote pass and the strong barbarians of the western border—not comparable to Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: "Lingwu is a remote pass against strong western barbarians—not Bohai."

sentences.zh: 苟許其專製，則無失事機，縱有營私冒利，民政不舉，亦乞不問。

translations.literal: If they are allowed sole discretion there is no lost opportunity; even if they seek private profit and civil affairs fail, I beg they not be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: "Grant discretion though they seek profit—do not question."

sentences.zh: 用將之術，異於他官，貪勇知愚，無不皆錄，但使法寬而人有所慕，則久居者安心展體，竭材盡慮，何患靈州之不可守哉？

translations.literal: The method of using generals differs from other offices; greedy, brave, wise, or foolish—all are recorded; only make the law broad so men admire it, then long-serving men rest easy, exhaust talent and thought—why fear Lingzhou cannot be held?
translations.idiomatic: "Using generals differs—record all types, make law broad, and Lingzhou can be held."

sentences.zh: 又朝廷比禁青鹽，甚為允愜。

translations.literal: Moreover the court recently banned green salt, which is very fitting.
translations.idiomatic: "The recent green-salt ban is fitting."

sentences.zh: 或聞議者欲開其禁。

translations.literal: I have heard some discussers wish to open the ban.
translations.idiomatic: "Some wish to open the ban."

sentences.zh: 且鹽之不入中土，困賊之良策也。

translations.literal: Salt not entering China is a fine strategy to distress the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: "Keeping salt from China distresses the enemy."

sentences.zh: 今若謂糧食自蕃界來，雖鹽禁不能困賊，此鬻鹽行賄者之妄談也。

translations.literal: Now if one says grain comes from tribal territory and the salt ban cannot distress the enemy, that is the wild talk of salt sellers who bribe.
translations.idiomatic: "Saying grain from tribes makes the salt ban useless is bribery talk."

sentences.zh: 蕃粟不入賊境，而入於邊廩，其利甚明。

translations.literal: Tribal grain not entering enemy territory but entering border granaries—the profit is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: "Tribal grain to our granaries, not the enemy's, profits clearly."

sentences.zh: 況漢地不食青鹽，熟戶亦不入蕃界博易，所禁者非徒糧食也，至於兵甲皮幹之物，其名益多。

translations.literal: Moreover Han territory does not eat green salt and settled households also do not go into tribal territory to trade; what is banned is not only grain but armor, hides, and the like—the names grow more.
translations.idiomatic: "We ban more than grain—armor, hides, and more; tribes must not feed the enemy."

sentences.zh: 以朝廷雄富，猶言摘山煮海，一年商利不入，則或闕軍須。

translations.literal: Though the court is rich it still says mining mountains and boiling sea—if one year's commercial profit does not enter, military needs may lack.
translations.idiomatic: "Though the court is rich, lost salt profit can cost military needs."

sentences.zh: 況蕃戎所賴，止在青鹽，禁之則彼自困矣。

translations.literal: What the barbarians rely on is only green salt; banning it then they are themselves distressed.
translations.idiomatic: "Barbarians rely on green salt; banning it distresses them."

sentences.zh: 望固守前詔為便。」

translations.literal: I hope the former edict be firmly kept as advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: "I hope the former edict stands."

sentences.zh: 五年，繼和領兵殺衛埋族於天麻川。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Jihe led troops and killed the Wei Mai tribe at Tianma valley.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Jihe killed the Wei Mai tribe at Tianma valley.

sentences.zh: 自是壟山外諸族皆恐懼內附，願於要害處置族帳砦柵，以為戍守。

translations.literal: From this tribes beyond Longshan all feared and submitted inward, asking to place clan stockades at strategic points for garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes beyond Longshan feared him and asked for garrison stockades.

sentences.zh: 繼和因請移涇原部署於鎮戎，以壯軍勢，又請開道環、延為應援。

translations.literal: Jihe therefore requested moving the Jingyuan deployer to Zhenrong to strengthen military power and also opening roads through Huan and Yan for reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Jihe asked to move the Jingyuan deployer to Zhenrong and open Huan and Yan roads.

sentences.zh: 真宗以其精心戎事，甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Zhenzong, because he devoted himself to border affairs, greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong greatly praised his border devotion.

sentences.zh: 戎人伺警巡馳備，一夕，塞長壕，越古長城抵城下。

translations.literal: The barbarians watched for patrols to relax; one night they filled the long moat, crossed the ancient Great Wall, and reached below the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians watched for lax patrols, filled the moat, crossed the Great Wall, and reached the wall.

sentences.zh: 繼和與都監史重貴出兵禦之，賊據險再突城隍，列陣接戰，重貴中重創，敗走之，大獲甲騎。

translations.literal: Jihe with overall supervisor Shi Chonggui led troops to resist; the enemy seized high ground and again rushed the wall and moat, arrayed and fought; Chonggui was heavily wounded; they routed them and took armor and horses in great number.
translations.idiomatic: Jihe and Shi Chonggui fought; Chonggui was wounded; they routed the enemy and took much armor and horses.

sentences.zh: 有詔嘉獎，別出良藥、縑帛、牢酒以賜。

translations.literal: There was an edict of praise; separately fine medicine, silk, good wine, and provisions were given.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him and sent medicine, silk, wine, and provisions.

sentences.zh: 繼和習武藝，好談方略，頗知書，所至幹治。

translations.literal: Jihe practiced martial arts, loved discussing strategy, knew books somewhat, and wherever he went governed effectively.
translations.idiomatic: Jihe was martial, strategic, literate, and effective in office.

sentences.zh: 然性剛忍，御下少恩，部兵終日擐甲，常如寇至；

translations.literal: Yet he was stubborn and cruel, showed little grace to subordinates; his troops wore armor all day as if enemies were coming;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was cruel to subordinates; troops wore armor all day as if under attack;

sentences.zh: 及較閱之際，杖罰過當，人多怨焉。

translations.literal: at inspection he punished excessively and many resented.
translations.idiomatic: at inspection he punished excessively and bred resentment.

sentences.zh: 真宗屢加勖勵，且為覆護之。

translations.literal: Zhenzong repeatedly encouraged him and also shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong encouraged and shielded him.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言：「保捷軍新到屯所，多亡命者，請優賜緡錢；

translations.literal: He once memorialized: "The Baojie army newly arrived at its garrison has many fugitives; please generously grant cash;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the new Baojie army had many deserters and asked for cash rewards;

sentences.zh: 苟有亡逸，即按軍法。」

translations.literal: if any flee, then apply military law."
translations.idiomatic: with desertion punished by military law."

sentences.zh: 舊制，凡賜軍中，雖緣奏請者，亦以特旨給之。

translations.literal: By old rule, even grants to the army requested by memorial were given by special edict.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule even requested army grants came by special edict.

sentences.zh: 上以繼和峻酷，欲軍士感其惠，特令以所奏著詔書中而加賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Jihe was harsh, wished the soldiers to feel his grace and specially ordered his memorial be written into the edict with added gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding Jihe harsh, wished soldiers to feel grace and added gifts in the edict per his memorial.

sentences.zh: 且以計情定罪，自有常制，不許其請。

translations.literal: Moreover judging guilt by circumstances has its regular rule—his request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Judging guilt by circumstance had fixed rules—his request was denied.

sentences.zh: 終以邊防之地，慮人不為用，遣張志言代還。

translations.literal: Finally because it was a border post, fearing men would not serve, Zhang Zhiyan was sent to replace him and recall him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing border troops would not serve, Zhang Zhiyan replaced him.

sentences.zh: 既即路，軍中皆恐其復來。

translations.literal: Once on the road the army all feared he would return.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure the army feared he would return.

sentences.zh: 六年，又出為幷、代鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again sent out as military controller of Bing and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was again military controller of Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 將行請對，欲領兵去按度邊壘。

translations.literal: About to depart he requested audience and wished to lead troops to inspect the border ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he sought audience to lead troops inspecting border works.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「河東岩險，兵甲甚眾，賊若入寇，但邀其歸路，自可致勝，不必率兵而往也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Hedong is rugged; arms are very numerous; if bandits invade, only cut off their return route and victory can naturally be won—there is no need to lead troops there."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Hedong was rugged and numerous in arms; if invaders came, cut their retreat—no need to lead troops there.

sentences.zh: 景德初，北邊入寇，徙北平砦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde the northern border was invaded and he was moved to Beiping stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde the north was invaded and he was moved to Beiping stockade.

sentences.zh: 車駕駐澶淵，繼和受詔與魏能、張凝領兵赴趙州躡敵後。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage halted at Chanyuan, Jihe received orders with Wei Neng and Zhang Ning to lead troops to Zhao Prefecture and follow the enemy's rear.
translations.idiomatic: At Chanyuan Jihe with Wei Neng and Zhang Ning trailed the enemy toward Zhao.

sentences.zh: 契丹請和，邊民猶未寧，又命副將張凝為緣邊巡檢安撫使。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sought peace the border people were still uneasy; he was again ordered as deputy overall inspector and pacification commissioner of the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan sought peace the border was uneasy; he was made deputy border pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 事平，復還幷、代。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he returned to Bing and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs settled he returned to Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷每詔書約束邊事，或有當行極斷之語，官吏不詳深意，即處大辟。

translations.literal: At the time every edict constrained border affairs; some had language of extreme execution; officials not understanding the deep intent immediately imposed capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts on border affairs sometimes mandated extreme execution; officials imposed capital punishment without understanding.

sentences.zh: 繼和言其事，乃詔：「自今有云重斷、極斷、處斬、決配之類，悉須裁奏。」

translations.literal: Jihe spoke of this; then an edict: "From now on where it says heavy execution, extreme execution, execution, or exile, all must be submitted for imperial decision."
translations.idiomatic: Jihe reported this; an edict required imperial decision for extreme punishments.

sentences.zh: 先是，繼隆卒，繼和恥以遺奏得官。

translations.literal: Earlier when Jilong died Jihe was ashamed to gain office from a leftover memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Jilong died Jihe was ashamed to gain office from a leftover memorial.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷西上閤門使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he became Western Upper Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢殿前都虞候、領端州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Deputy Commander of the Palace Hall Army and Defender of Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Deputy Commander of the Palace Hall Army and Defender of Duan.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 1 he died at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮國軍節度，遣諸王率宗室素服赴吊。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made military commissioner of the Zhenguo army; the princes were ordered to lead the clan in plain dress to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously Zhenguo military commissioner; princes led clan mourning in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 二子早卒。

translations.literal: Two sons died young.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons died young.

sentences.zh: 帝以其族盛大，諸侄皆幼，令三班選使臣為主家事。

translations.literal: The emperor, because his clan was large and the nephews all young, ordered the Three Class to choose an envoy to manage household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His clan being large and nephews young, the emperor chose an envoy to manage the household.

sentences.zh: 弟繼恂，至洛苑使、順州刺史，贈左神武大將軍。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jixun reached Commissioner of the Luoyuan and prefect of Shunzhou and was posthumously made Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Jixun became Luoyuan Commissioner and Shunzhou prefect, posthumously Left Divine Martial Grand General.

sentences.zh: 子昭遜為供備庫使。

translations.literal: Son Zhaoxun was Commissioner of the Supply Preparation Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhaoxun was Supply Preparation Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 論曰：夫乘風雲之會，依日月之光，感慨發憤，效忠駿奔，居備要任，出握重兵，如是而令名克終，斯固可偉也。

translations.literal: Discussion says: Those who ride the meeting of wind and cloud, rely on sun and moon light, are stirred to loyal urgency and swift service, hold crucial posts and grasp heavy armies—if they thus keep good name to the end, that is indeed admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: Those who seize their age, serve in crisis, hold power and armies, and end with a good name are admirable.

sentences.zh: 吳廷祚策李筠之破，如目睹其事，誠有將略。

translations.literal: Wu Tingzuo foresaw Li Jing's defeat as if he saw it with his own eyes—he truly had military acumen.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingzuo foresaw Li Jing's defeat as if he saw it—truly a strategist.

sentences.zh: 李崇矩秉純厚之德，感史弘肇之恩，保其叛亡之孥，然交鄭伸不知其傾險，坐謫炎海，固無先見之明矣；

translations.literal: Li Chongju held pure generous virtue, was moved by Shi Hongzhao's grace, protected the children of his rebel and fugitive, yet in befriending Zheng Shen did not know his treacherous danger and was banished to the southern sea—he truly lacked foresight;
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongju was generous and protected Shi Hongzhao's fugitive kin, yet befriending treacherous Zheng Shen he was banished south—he lacked foresight;

sentences.zh: 其子繼昌，忘父仇以恤伸母之貧，雖非中道，亦人所難。

translations.literal: his son Jichang forgot his father's enmity to relieve Shen's mother's poverty—though not the middle way, it is what men find hard.
translations.idiomatic: yet his son Jichang forgot enmity to aid Shen's mother—though not orthodox, it was hard to do.

sentences.zh: 王仁贍征蜀，殺降附之卒，肆貪矯之行，鬱鬱而斃，自貽伊戚，尚何尤乎？

translations.literal: Wang Renshan on the Shu campaign killed surrendering soldiers and indulged greedy false conduct, died resentful—he brought trouble on himself; what complaint remains?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renshan killed surrendering troops in Shu, grew greedy, and died resentful—he brought it on himself.

sentences.zh: 楚昭輔當陳橋推戴，太祖遣之入安母后，亦必可託以事者；

translations.literal: Chu Zhaofu at Chenqiao's acclamation—Taizu sent him to reassure the empress dowager—he too was one who could be entrusted with affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Zhaofu at Chenqiao was sent to reassure the empress dowager—one who could be trusted;

sentences.zh: 及為三司，善於心計，人不可干以私，然終以訐直，取寡信之名，何歟？

translations.literal: when he was head of the Three Departments he was skilled at accounting and none dared seek private favors from him, yet in the end he gained a name for stinginess and little trust—why?
translations.idiomatic: as Three Departments head he was skilled at accounts and incorruptible, yet ended with a name for stinginess—why?

sentences.zh: 處耘於創業之始，功參締構，克荊山，靖衡、湘，勢如拉枯，而志昧在和，勳業弗究，良可惜也；

translations.literal: Chuyun at the founding's beginning shared in establishment, took Jing mountain, pacified Heng and Xiang, momentum like snapping dry wood, yet his aim was unclear on harmony and merit was not completed—deeply regrettable;
translations.idiomatic: Chuyun at the founding helped build the state and swept Jinghu, yet lacked harmony and left merit incomplete—regrettable;

sentences.zh: 幸聯戚畹之貴，秉旄繼世，抑造物之報，嗇此而豐彼歟？

translations.literal: fortunately linked by imperial marriage, holding banners generation after generation—is it that the Creator's reward is sparing here and lavish there?
translations.idiomatic: yet by imperial marriage his house held command generation after generation—did Heaven spare here to lavish there?
